| `emit_block` barrier hoisting | unrecognised statement → keep scanning past it, and no dependency check | arithmetic moved above the barrier its operands come from, emitting undefined PTX symbols — and it was reordering around `barrier_sync()`, which emitted no barrier |
| `zk_emitter::emit_block` | `return` recorded, not obeyed — last one wins | `if c { return x; } return y;` emitted a circuit computing `y` unconditionally; Z3 proved the output was a constant |
| `zk_emitter` `Stmt::If` | missing branch's return → `LinearCombination::zero` | the fall-through value was 0 instead of whatever follows the `if` |
| `zk_emitter` `Stmt::If` | condition used as a selector, never constrained to a bit | `if a { 5 } else { 9 }` emitted `9 - 4a`; `a = 2` gave 1, which neither branch returns |
| `zk_emitter` `Stmt::If`, one-sided return | fall-through muxed against the ENCLOSING block's tail, so a nested `if` reported its own empty tail's zero | `if c { if d { return 1; } } return 7;` emitted 0; found by writing the semantics down in Coq, not by testing |
| `zk_emitter` `Stmt::For` | loop body's return value discarded entirely | `for i in 0..4 { if c { return 1; } } return 9;` emitted the constant 9 |
| `zk_emitter` constant folding | gadget fast paths skipped the 32-bit range check the gadget enforces | `v >= 31 * 2^32` folded to a 254-bit `Fr` ordering; `0 - 1 >= 0` folded to **true** |
| `ptx_emitter` intrinsic arity | missing argument → `else { "%r0" }` / `"%rd0"` / `"%f0"` | a short call read an unrelated variable's register: `block_ptr2d_store` with 5 of 7 args made the stored VALUE the bounds limit, emitting `setp.lt.u32 %p0, %r6, %f0` |
| `llvm_emitter` `emit_type` | `U64`/`U32`/`U8`/`U16`/`I8` absent → `_ => "i32"` | `let x: U64 = ...` allocated an **i32**; the store truncated and clang accepted it |
| `llvm_emitter` `infer_type` | every `IntLit` → `"i32"` regardless of value | `let a: I64 = 3000000000; a > 0` **returned false** — the literal was built as i32 and sign-extended. Compiles, links, runs, wrong |
| `ptx_emitter` unknown call name | any unmatched `fname` → `""` | `store(A, 0, made_up(t), ...)` emitted `setp.lt.u32 %p1, , %r0;` — a missing operand — under a green banner; caught only when bound with `let` |
| `ptx_emitter` `mbarrier_*` | 1-arg call missed an `args.len() >= 2` guard → no branch → `""` | a barrier that emitted **nothing**, listed as SUPPORTED because empty PTX assembles; the 2-arg form writes `%rd0` (a parameter) and needs sm_90 under an sm_89 target |
| `ptx_emitter` `mma_sync` | 3 fragment args discarded; one fixed `mma.sync` with wrong register counts | `%f1` outside the declared `.reg .f32 %f<1>` pool and 2 accumulator regs where m16n8k16 needs 4 — **the `wgmma_async` bug, missed by the sweep that fixed it** |
| `ptx_emitter` `block_arange` | `(start, len)` discarded, always `%tid.x` | a non-zero start silently produced the wrong index; it assembles, so the substring test guarding it never noticed |
| `ptx_emitter` `GlobalMemory::load` | arguments discarded, address hardcoded to `[%rd0]` | assembles, launches, reads parameter 0 whatever you passed — `tests/train_spec.ysu` asks for `GlobalMemory::load(weights)` and would have got a different buffer |
| `cpu_emitter` `emit_expr` | `_ => "0 // Fallback"` | `a + b` became the **constant 0** - `Expr::BinaryOp` was never handled. The trailing `//` also commented out the rest of the line, *including the statement's terminator* |
| `cpu_emitter` `emit_block` | `_ => {}` | `if`, `while`, `+=` and `break` silently DROPPED, so a loop body vanished and the function returned its initial value - in Rust that still compiles |
| `native_emitter` `Expr::Ident` | name discarded, always `mov eax, [rbp-4]` | every identifier read the FIRST local: `let a=9; let b=2; return a - b;` emitted a runnable ELF returning **0** |
| `native_emitter` `BinaryOp` | `_ => {}` | `/`, `%`, all six comparisons, `&`/`\|`/`^` and both shifts emitted **no instruction**, leaving the left operand in `eax` - `9 / 2` returned **9** |
| `native_emitter` params | argument registers never spilled | a function with parameters read stack garbage; nothing stored `rdi`/`rsi`/... anywhere |
| `ptx_emitter::emit_stmt` | `_ => {}` for `While`/`Break`/`Match`, and `Stmt::Return(_, _) => {}` | a `while` loop's whole body vanished — the kernel assembles, launches, and stores its pre-loop value; a bare `return;` was an early exit that silently did not happen |
| `ptx_emitter::emit_expr` `_ => "".into()` | a string literal in an argument position → an empty operand | `mul.lo.s32 %r5, , %r1;` and `setp.lt.u32 %p0, , %r2;` under "Compilation Successful!" and exit 0; `ptxas` rejects the file with a parse error, on a machine that is not the one that compiled it |
| `ptx_emitter::emit_expr` `Expr::MemberAccess` | anything not a `v4` lane or `.wait` → `"".into()` | `x.lane` in an argument position emitted `cvt.rn.f32.s32 %f1, ;` under "Compilation Successful!" and exit 0 — **the same hole that was closed for `Expr::Ident`, for `Expr::BoolLit` and for the `_` arm, and never for this one** |
| `ptx_emitter::emit_expr` `Expr::Ident` | an unbound name → `name.clone()` | `let z: u32 = ZeroInit;` emitted `mov.u32 %r0, ZeroInit;` — `ptxas` answers `Unknown symbol`. Every name this backend defines is in `variables`, so a bare name means the program named something absent |
| `ptx_emitter::emit_expr` `Expr::BoolLit` | **no arm at all**, so `if true` fell to `_ => ""` and was REFUSED | the fail-closed direction of the same hole — it took out `Y tests/test_drift.ysu --emit-ptx`, a documented command an earlier session had already repaired once |
| `type_checker` loop intervals | body-assigned variables cleared BEFORE the initiation check, not between initiation and preservation | every `@invariant` naming a variable its body assigns failed initiation, so `while` was unusable in safe Y and two of the repo's own test programs were refused |
| `native_emitter` integer width | `emit32(*val as u32)` for every literal, and a 32-bit datapath under a declared `I64` | `let a: I64 = 100000; let b: I64 = 100000; return (a * b) >> 32;` answered **0** where the answer is 2 — in a RUNNABLE ELF, exit 0, "Compiled to native ELF executable!" |
| `zk_emitter::emit_stmt` | `_ => {}` for `CompoundAssign` | `let x = a; x += 5; return x;` emitted the single constraint `w_1 * 1 = w_2`, i.e. a circuit computing `out = a`, which Groth16 proves as readily as the right one |
| `zk_emitter::emit_stmt` | `_ => {}` for `SafeBlock`/`GhostBlock`/`Chisel`/`ClockDomainBlock` | `@ghost { x = x + 5; }` dropped whole; every other backend lowers these as ordinary blocks |
| `type_checker` `Stmt::Match` | a branch that never raised the linear tracker's conditional depth | `if n { pipe.wait(t); }` was rejected and `match n { _ => pipe.wait(t) }` - the same program - compiled clean |
| `type_checker` `takes_reference` | consulted at ONE site (top-level `Stmt::Expr`), and `_ => false` for `StructLit` | `if c { bump(&i); }`, `y = bump(&i);`, `let y = bump(&i);`, a `match` arm and `bump(P { x: &i })` all compiled clean with the `@invariant` "verified" against a variable the callee was free to overwrite |
| `type_checker::collect_assigned` | `_ => {}` | the havoc set for a branch, so a missed name keeps its stale version and preservation gets strictly EASIER |
| `ir_grapher::analyze_stmt` | `_ => {}` for 7 of 17 `Stmt` variants | `b += bvh_traverse(a)` graphed **0 cross-pipeline edges** where `b = bvh_traverse(a)` graphs 1, so the scheduler emitted **0 sync barriers** — the Tensor consumer reads the RT producer's shared memory unsynchronised, and the FP32→FP16 conversion is never emitted either, because both hang off `cross_pipeline_edges()` |
| `ir_grapher::wire_expr_dependencies` | `_ => {}` for `StructLit`/`MemberAccess`/`GenericCall`/`BlockExpr` | a read reaching a consumer through a struct field built no edge, so the consumer could be scheduled before its producer |

**PHASE 0 IS DONE: the exact `vpdpwssd` GEMM is substituted for a recognised nest and is BIT-IDENTICAL to the naive one.** The licence logic, the micro-kernel, both packers and the threaded driver all already existed — `emit_vnni_gemm_module`'s only caller was a test, and `try_emit_gemm_kernel` reported "LICENSED but not yet implemented" and returned `None`. Wiring that one call is what `docs/proof_carrying_kernels.md` calls "make the two halves meet".
  - **The operand domain is the SOURCE'S TYPES, and that is the decision the whole thing turned on.** `VnniExact::license` is stated over "the int16 operand values actually fed to `vpdpwssd`". An `F32` nest cannot reach that domain without a quantization scale — at which point the licence would have been granted against the source's magnitude and not the kernel's, which is the unsoundness fixed one commit earlier. Declaring the buffers `I16` with an `I64` accumulator *is* the kernel's contract, so nothing is converted and there is no scale to get wrong. An `F32` `@ZeroDrift` nest still falls back to scalar exact lowering, permanently.
  - **THE PRODUCT MUST NOT TRUNCATE, and this is the check that makes the substitution legal rather than merely fast.** `let a_val: I16` makes `a_val * b_val` an **i16 multiply** — 1024*1024 is 2^20, so it overflows — and the naive nest accumulates the truncated product (`mul i16` then `sext i16 ... to i64` in the emitted IR). `vpdpwssd` widens internally, so substituting it there replaces a truncating reduction with a widening one: a different function, computed faster, under a certificate claiming exactness. Refused by name, naming the repair (`I64` operand `let`s sign-extend at the load).
  - **`sum = sum + x` on a `@ZeroDrift` accumulator was MIS-LOWERED, and it is the form the GEMM recogniser matches.** Only `+=` had a drift-aware arm, so the running-sum form fell through to the ordinary assignment path: read via `sitofp`, add in `double`, then **`store double` into an `alloca i64`**. Pointers are untyped in LLVM, so `clang` accepts it and the next read interprets the double's BIT PATTERN as an integer — 2,896,931 came back as −4,337,501,956,902,952,448. Same shape as the ZK emitter's `x += 5` versus `x = x + 5` in the design-rule table, found here in the *other* direction. Any other assignment to a drift accumulator is now refused rather than converted.
    - **The arm had to be placed ABOVE the general `Stmt::Assign`.** Inserted below it, it compiled, ran, and never fired — match arms are ordered, and a more specific arm added after a general one is dead code that nothing reports.
  - **Both bugs were found by building the differential FIRST and running it**, within minutes of the wiring compiling. Neither is visible in the emitted IR to a reader: one is a legal `mul i16`, the other is legal-but-mismatched `store double`. This is the strongest argument in the repo for `feedback-cross-backend-differential`, applied to an optimisation rather than to a backend.
  - The verification runs both readings of the same source over six shapes including ragged ones, checks each against an independent integer reference, and compares the two for **EQUALITY**. The driver poisons `C` with `0xAB` first, because the kernel accumulates INTO it (that is what lets a caller split K across threads) while the nest it replaces assigns — a missing memset would otherwise hide behind a `calloc`.
  - **The K-split across threads is done too (`__y_gemm_exact_vnni_threaded`, `tests/exact_gemm_thread_invariance.rs`)**: byte-identical output at 1, 2, 3, 5, 8 and 16 threads over a ragged K, each run also checked against an integer reference. Plain `pthread_create`/`join` rather than the f32 path's persistent pool — that pool is tuned around a task struct shaped for that kernel, and forking per call is noise at any size where threading pays. 37.7 -> 10.2 ms at 8 threads on 256x256x65536, identical checksum throughout. The wrapper owns the zeroing of `C`, because the kernel accumulates INTO it (which is what makes the bands summable) while the nest it replaces assigns.
    - **"Same answer at every thread count" is ALSO what a threading path that never spawns a thread reports** — a no-op is perfectly invariant. The bit-identity assertion is therefore paired with a liveness canary counting real `pthread_create` calls through `-Wl,--wrap=pthread_create`: deterministic, unlike a timing check, and it reports 0 at one thread (the direct path) and exactly N at N. `feedback-null-metrics-pass-dead-components`, in the place it matters most.
    - **K is 4099 in that test on purpose.** The band floor (`KSPLIT_MIN_BAND`, 128) caps the thread count at `K/128`, so at the K values the correctness tests use (~300) a sweep to 16 threads would silently be a sweep to **2** — `feedback-exercised-is-not-covered`. Mutation-verified 4/4 with distinct diagnoses: collapsing the split fails the canary; dropping the remainder distribution, skipping a partial, and failing to shift B by `k0*ldb` each fail against the reference.
    - **Libc declarations are emitted only when the f32 module is absent.** It declares the same entry points, and a duplicate `declare` is an **invalid redefinition** in LLVM rather than a duplicate that gets merged. Both modules in one program is a case that now occurs and is checked.
  - **Phase 0's "both backends" clause is NOT met and its premise is false**, recorded in the roadmap rather than quietly treated as covered. `--emit-cpu` cannot express the recognised nest at all — it refuses `block_ptr2d_load` by name — and its GEMM kernels come from a *different mechanism*: a shape dispatcher keyed on literal `M`/`N`/`K` emitting hand-written Rust/AVX, with **zero** `@ZeroDrift` references in the whole file. Satisfying it means writing a second exact GEMM in Rust source form for a backend Y never compiles.

**The compiler can now be asked for BOTH readings of one source, and that pair is a differential nothing else in the repo performs (`tests/gemm_substitution_differential.rs`).** `recognize_gemm` matches `sum += A[i,k]*B[k,j]` and substitutes a tiled, packed, threaded kernel — which is exactly the claim `docs/proof_carrying_kernels.md` exists to eventually prove. `Y_NO_GEMM_RECOGNISER=1` lowers the nest as written instead, so the same source compiled twice gives the optimized kernel and the naive nest it claims to equal.
  - **The oracle is the compiler's own lowering, not a reference typed into a test.** Every other GEMM test here checks the substituted kernel against a hand-written C reference — a good oracle with one weakness: it is a second implementation of the language's semantics and can drift from what the source means. This one cannot disagree with the language, because it *is* the language.
  - **It also closes a gap nothing else covered: the naive lowering is executed by no other test.** Every existing GEMM test runs the substituted path, so a bug in ordinary loop/index/load lowering was invisible to all of them.
  - **Three-way, not two-way.** Two implementations that agree can be wrong together and a differential would report a clean run, so each arm is ALSO checked against an f64 reference in the driver — f64 rather than reordered f32, so it is genuinely independent.
  - **The comparison is a TOLERANCE and that is not a compromise, it is the thesis.** f32 addition is not associative, so a tiled reduction provably does not equal the naive one bit for bit — which is the whole reason kernel verification is considered impractical and the reason exact accumulation is the programme's foundation. `the_exact_path_is_still_unsubstituted_so_the_tolerance_above_is_still_right` asserts the emitter does NOT yet substitute an exact kernel, and **fails deliberately when Phase 0's wiring lands**: integer addition IS associative, so an exact substituted kernel must be bit-identical and a tolerance would accept one that is merely close.
  - **`Y_NO_GEMM_RECOGNISER` persists into whatever artifacts are written while it is set**, exactly like `Y_CTA_OVERRIDE` and `Y_SWIGLU_TILE`. It makes Y slow, never wrong — but a `.ll` regenerated under it contains the naive nest and no packed kernel.
  - Mutation-verified: an off-by-one in the packed micro-tile's row count (`iw`) is caught at relative L2 **0.42**, and both non-vacuity controls fire — one arm not substituted means the test compared a program against itself.
  - **A process note worth more than the test.** `git checkout src/llvm_emitter.rs`, used to revert a mutation, silently discarded the UNCOMMITTED call site the whole feature depends on; the suite still passed because the remaining half compiled and the switch simply never fired. Revert a mutation by restoring the file you saved, not by reaching for git on a file with uncommitted work in it.

**The exact-VNNI licence certified operands it cannot represent, and a CONJUNCTION check is what found it (`tests/exact_gemm_licence_obligations.rs`).** `VnniExact::license` is Phase 0's soundness core — the predicate saying a tiled, threaded, K-split GEMM may use `vpdpwssd` and still be bit-identical to the naive nest. Its own doc says `m` is "in the scheme's own integer domain … **not** the real-valued range of the source matrices", and that converting between them "is the caller's job precisely because getting it wrong is a wrong answer rather than a slow one". **The caller does not do it**: `DriftAccumulator::operand_bounds` takes `max(|lo|,|hi|)` of the user's `@bounds` — real numbers — and passes them straight through. `@bounds(-0.001, 0.001)` was LICENSED at magnitude 0.001, and every such operand stages to int16 **zero**; the kernel would compute the zero matrix under a licence certifying exactness.
  - **It has never shipped a wrong answer for exactly one reason: the kernel is not wired in.** `plan_exact_gemm` produces a `drift_report` advisory ("LICENSED but not yet implemented") and the emitter falls back to scalar exact lowering. This is a licence that becomes a wrong answer the moment Phase 0's wiring lands — i.e. when nobody is looking at it. **Find these while the path is still dead, not after.**
  - **EXHAUST, do not model, when the domain is finite.** The operand magnitude lives in int16, so its whole domain is 32,768 values: calling the real function over every input it can receive is *complete* rather than sampled, and closes the model-versus-code gap a solver would leave open (`proofs/ZkControlFlow.v` states that gap about itself). Z3 earns its place only where an axis is unbounded — here K, which gets stated integer arithmetic and a written-down ceiling (~5.5e11) that existed nowhere before and MOVES if the flush interval or either width changes. Same shape as the attention path's "hard context ceiling written down nowhere".
  - **The boundary is one unit wide**: at T=64, 4095 fits with 1,048,447 to spare and 4096 exceeds `i32::MAX` by EXACTLY ONE. An off-by-one in the `floor(sqrt(..))` derivation is invisible to any sampled test.
  - **`flush_interval_for` is consulted only to phrase an error message** — `plan_exact_gemm` passes `DEFAULT_FLUSH_K_PAIRS` unconditionally. A first probe checked the selector/checker pair and came back perfectly clean **because it was checking a path that does not ship**. Establish which configuration actually reaches the user before sweeping it.
  - **One mutation was a hole in my own test.** Asserting `license(32768.0).is_err()` passed with the int16 width check DELETED: `max_operand_magnitude` never exceeds `i16::MAX`, so the overflow branch refuses everything the width branch would. It asserts WHICH diagnosis is given now — that is all the width check decides, and "does not fit int16" is a different repair from "can overflow the int32 accumulator", which would send a user to tune a flush interval that cannot fix a width.

**THE int8 GEMM WAS CALLED A STUB FROM A GREP, AND ITS LAUNCH CONTRACT GAVE A WRONG ANSWER (`src/ptx_emitter.rs`, `proofs/Int8GemmSchedule.v`, `tests/int8_gemm_launch_contract.rs`).** Taken from the previous increment's own residue, which named the int8 bring-up as the next item and said to measure what it costs before writing any of it. The measurement moved the plan twice. **144 / 622 / 0 default, 144 / 873 / 0 zk, 4 / 8 / 0 y-gpu - exactly +1 target and +3 tests in each of the first two, which is this change and nothing else; 138 targets swept separately in both feature sets, 0 bad; all three builds warning-free; corpus unchanged at `--emit-ptx` 60/25, `--emit-llvm` 55/30, `--emit-cpu` 46/39; the only committed artifacts touched are the two int8 `.ptx`, whose diff is exactly the guard plus label renumbering.** Commit `cfbced6`, pushed.
  - **CORRECTED BY THE ENTRY BELOW: the two baseline figures in this entry are WRONG.** cuBLASLt is **144,196** not 38,090 (`.contiguous()` was inside the timed loop) and the ISA ceiling is **179,761** not 374,027 (the probe stored one of eight accumulator sets, and a doubling control cannot see that). So Y is **0.09x** not 0.41x, and **8%** of the ceiling not 4%. The Y column reproduces; only the baselines moved. Kept as written with this pointer, because the errors are the more useful half.
  - **THE "STUB" CLAIM WAS A GREP AND THE GREP WAS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT.** The previous entry counted `cp.async`/`ldmatrix`/`bar.sync` occurrences (89 lines, 2 mma, zero of each) against the f16 kernel's 964/65/22/24/7 and concluded stub. Measured at 4096^3, clock-ramped, every timed configuration correctness-checked: **15,439 G MAC/s, 0.41x cuBLASLt's `torch._int_mm` (38,090)**. A 0.41x kernel is not a stub. Second time this session that a structural grep produced a confident wrong claim - the other was "zero floating point in the SASS", which omitted `HFMA2`.
  - **THE FIRST TIMING RUN WAS 4x SLOW ACROSS THE BOARD AND REPORTED NOTHING WRONG.** This card idles far below boost and the recorded window effect ("absolute timings moved 4-5x between windows") applies. What made it visible was arithmetic, not suspicion: 4096 reported 2,724 GB/s of A/B traffic against a ~672 GB/s card, which is not physical. **A ramp phase plus a correctness check on every timed configuration is what makes the numbers reproduce** - and the correctness check is the null-metric guard, since a kernel that does no work is very fast.
  - **THE ISA CEILING IS ONLY QUOTABLE BECAUSE OF ITS CONTROL.** int8 `mma.sync.m16n8k32` measures **374,027 G MAC/s**, doubling-verified (ratio 2.000) with 32 live `IMMA.16832.S8.S8` in the disassembly. That is **4x** the f16 rate where a spec-sheet reading predicts 2x. Recorded as measured and unreconciled rather than adjusted, because **the identical probe in f16 reads 92,482 G MAC/s = 185 TFLOPS against this card's ~176 spec** - the arm whose answer is independently known validates the accounting method, and the int8 arm uses it unchanged. *When a measurement disagrees with a spec sheet, run the same instrument on a case whose answer you already know rather than adjusting the number.*
  - **WHERE THE 0.41x GOES, ESTABLISHED BY A PREDICTION THAT CAME TRUE.** Neither kernel is compute bound (4.1% and 10.2% of the ceiling). Y's has no shared staging - one warp reads its 16 A rows and 8 B columns straight from global, **0.1875 bytes per MAC**. Warp-level read traffic: 2048^3 **2,821 GB/s**, 4096^3 **2,887**, 6144^3 **2,905**, then 8192^3 **789 GB/s** and throughput **collapses 3.7x** (15,496 -> 4,209) once the working set leaves the 48 MB L2. Flat then a cliff is the signature of a bandwidth roof, and the cliff was predicted from the byte count before it was run. A 128x128 staged tile moves 2/128 bytes per MAC, **12x less** - so the bring-up is worth ~2.5x at L2-resident shapes and ~9x beyond, with a mechanism instead of a guess.
  - **THE FINDING: THE SCHEDULE GIVES ONE TILE TO ONE WARP AND NOTHING CHECKED THE BLOCK SIZE.** The emitted kernel contained **one predicate** - the K-loop bound - and never mentioned `%ntid.x`. At M=64 N=32 K=128 with A=3 and B=5, so every output must be K*15 = 1920: block (32,1,1) correct; **(64,1,1) 1344 of 2048 wrong with `C[256] = 3840`**; (128,1,1) the same **and it reads row 79 of a 64-row A**. 3840 is **exactly double**, which is the mechanism: warp 1's `g = tid/4` lands in 8..15 instead of 0..7, so its two A-row reads are `cy*16+g` and `cy*16+g+8` - the second in the NEXT tile - and `red.global.add.s32` sums that second product into the same output.
    - **THIS IS THE ONE KERNEL WHOSE ADVERTISED CLAIM A WRONG BLOCK SIZE FALSIFIES.** `tests/gpu_batch_invariance.rs` asserts a bit-identical answer at every launch geometry. Same class as the `attn_scores` finding and the paged-decode contract, and worse in that respect: there the contract is at least written down.
    - Fixed with a **warp-uniform** guard (`tid >= 32`, constant across any warp, so `mma.sync.aligned` still sees all 32 lanes of warp 0 converged), branching past both the mma and the reduction. Every block size correct; cost is nothing measurable (15,061 vs 15,072 G MAC/s at 2048^3, inside the ~4% band).

Three claims, two schemas instantiated rather than re-derived: the guard's confinement (with its dual refuting the measured `g = 8` case); the striped split-K, which is residue classes so `GridStrideSplit`'s `grid_stride_exact` and **`atomics_may_land_in_any_order`** apply verbatim; and the output tiling plus lane decomposition, `MixedRadix`'s **fifth and sixth** consumers. The emitter asserts order-independence in a prose comment ("the same result for every grid, every launch, every scheduling accident") and nothing had checked it - `gpu_batch_invariance` sweeps seven split factors, which is seven points rather than a property.

That is not a gap in cuBLASLt - **integer accumulation is associative, so ANY int8 GEMM has the property for free**. The differentiator is not having it; it is having it **proved and stated**. (What cuBLASLt does not do is accept the shapes: `_int_mm` refuses M < 16 outright.)

**THE INT8 GEMM IS 4.29x FASTER WITH NO SHARED MEMORY, AND TWO NUMBERS I PUBLISHED TWO DAYS AGO WERE WRONG (`src/ptx_emitter.rs`, `proofs/Int8GemmSchedule.v`, `tests/int8_gemm_launch_contract.rs`).** Taken from the previous increment's own residue, which named the shared-memory staging as the next item and - per the standing discipline - said to measure what the bring-up costs before writing any of it. **The measurement moved the plan twice.** **144 / 625 / 0 default, 144 / 876 / 0 zk, 4 / 8 / 0 y-gpu - exactly +3 tests and +0 targets in each of the first two, which is this change and nothing else; 138 targets swept separately in both feature sets, 0 bad; both builds warning-free; corpus unchanged at `--emit-ptx` 60/25, `--emit-llvm` 55/30, `--emit-cpu` 46/39; the only committed artifacts touched are the two int8 `.ptx`.**
  - **THERE IS A CHEAPER LEVER POINTING THE SAME WAY, AND THE STAGING FRAMING HID IT.** One warp owned a 16x8 output tile and read its 16 A rows and 8 B columns straight from global: `768` bytes per 32-wide K step for 4096 MACs, **0.1875 B/MAC**, against a 128x128 staged CTA tile's `2/128` - a 12x gap that reads as "you need `cp.async`, `ldmatrix`, `bar.sync` and a multi-stage pipeline". **It is not one lever.** Issuing `mt*nt` mma per K step FROM THE SAME A AND B FRAGMENTS amortises both halves with no shared memory, no barrier and **no instruction this backend does not already emit**: a 64x64 warp tile is 0.0312 B/MAC, **6x**, i.e. HALF the staged pipeline's win for none of its machinery. Measured, same session, interleaved, ramped, every configuration correctness-checked: **4096^3 14,571 -> 61,374 (4.21x)**, **8192^3 4,912 -> 38,897 (7.92x)**, and through the real compiler old-emitter-against-new in one process **14,322 -> 61,441, 4.29x**. 199 registers, **`STACK:0 LOCAL:0` - zero spill**, which is what makes the 4x8 cap right rather than chosen. **But the obvious selector is a 7x REGRESSION at small shapes - see below.**
  - **BOTH BASELINES I PUBLISHED WERE WRONG, BY DIFFERENT MECHANISMS, AND THEY PARTLY CANCELLED.** Re-measuring them is what "cross-session numbers do not compose" asks for and both moved: **cuBLASLt 38,090 -> 144,196** and **the int8 mma ISA ceiling 374,027 -> 179,761**. The Y arm reproduces (15,439 -> 14,571). *A ratio whose two arms move by different factors between sessions has a CONTAMINATED arm, not a noisy one* - this repo's own OpenBLAS lesson, applied to my own figure from two days earlier.
    - **The baseline was low because `.contiguous()` sat inside the timed loop**, materialising a 16 MB copy per call. Identified rather than guessed: `_int_mm(A, B.t().contiguous())` measures **31,452**, essentially the published 38,090. The real kernel is `cutlass_80_tensorop_i16832gemm_s8_256x128_64x3_tn_align16`, read out of the profiler.
    - **THE CEILING IS THE MORE INTERESTING FAILURE, BECAUSE ITS CONTROL PASSED.** The probe kept eight accumulator sets and **stored one**, so `ptxas` deleted the seven dead mma chains - and the doubling control read a clean **2.000** anyway, because **A CONSTANT DEAD FRACTION DIVIDES OUT OF A RATIO.** What caught it was arithmetic, not suspicion: 374,027 is **2.1x above `66 SM x 2.61 GHz x 1024 MAC/SM/cycle`**, which is not physical. Storing every accumulator gives 179,761 - **102% of that bound** and **1.94x the f16 ceiling, exactly the 2x a spec sheet predicts.** *A doubling control proves work scales with the loop body, not that the loop body is live; the liveness control is that every result is stored.*
    - **THE TELL WAS WRITTEN DOWN AND FILED AS A CURIOSITY.** The original note recorded int8 at **4.04x** f16 where a spec sheet says 2x and called it "measured and unreconciled rather than adjusted". Refusing to fudge a number was right; **not chasing a 2x disagreement was not.** A measurement that disagrees with a spec sheet by 2x is a bug report. And the paragraph's own control - the f16 arm reading 185 TFLOPS against ~176 spec - was sound and was run on **the arm where the bug did not bite**: an accounting method validated on one arm does not validate another arm's dead-code elimination.
    - **THE CORRECTION CHANGED THE CONCLUSION, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT OF RE-MEASURING.** Under the published baseline, 4.29x on 0.41x reads as **1.56x cuBLASLt - "we beat the vendor library with no shared memory"**. That is false. Under the real baseline it is **0.09x -> 0.40x**: large, cheap, real, and **it does not close the gap**; the staged pipeline is still needed.
  - **THE LARGEST TILE IS A 7x LOSS AT A SMALL SHAPE, AND ONLY SWEEPING FOUND IT.** Taking the biggest tile the shape admits is the obvious rule and it is **wrong**: a tile is one WARP, so a 64x64 tile on a 64x64 matrix is one warp for the whole GEMM. Measured against the shipped 16x8 schedule, three runs agreeing to within 1%: **64x64 0.14x, 128x128 0.18x, 256x256 0.42x, 512x256 0.74x**, crossing over at 512x512 (1.62x) and 1024x1024 (3.13x). So the big tile is taken only when it leaves **>= 64 output tiles** - roughly one warp per SM - and otherwise the schedule stays at one mma per warp. **The fallback is to 16x8 OUTRIGHT rather than to the next size down**, because the intermediate tiles do not win either: at 256x256 the largest tile leaving 64 tiles is 32x32 and it measures **0.89x**. Validated on 14 shapes, 8 not used to derive the rule and including rectangular and decode-shaped ones: **worst case 1.00x - it never regresses** - while keeping 1.57-3.62x wherever the win exists. The 16x8 path is unchanged in cost by the tile loop (**0.99x**), which matters because the floor sends every small shape there. The constant is a **PERFORMANCE fallback, not a correctness one** (every tile the selector can return computes the same matrix), so it is fixed rather than probed - *a compiler that probes the local machine bakes that machine into its output*, and this decision does not need to. **The measurement is the increment: the obvious selector would have been a 7x regression on exactly the decode shapes an inference compiler cares about, and no correctness test could ever have said so.**
  - **THE SCHEDULE CHANGE FORCED A STRONGER PROPERTY THAN IT NEEDED, AND THAT IS THE PREVIOUS INCREMENT'S DEFECT ONE AXIS OVER.** The warp tile is a compile-time function of M and N, so it is **invisible at the call site** - a host still launching the pre-tiling `(N/8, M/16, z)` grid would start `mt*nt` times too many CTAs, each computing a base row `ty*(mt*16)` **at or past the end of the matrix**, with `red.global.add.s32` writing it. So the output tiles are **grid-strided in x and y**, the way K already was in z: every grid of at least (1,1,1) is correct, an over-large grid idles its extras, and **the pre-tiling host launch still computes the right matrix** - verified on the real compiler's 4096^3 output, where it is not merely correct but marginally faster (67,568 vs 61,441). The kernel is now invariant to block size, grid AND split factor. **A compile-time schedule choice that changes a launch contract must be paired with making the contract not matter.**
  - **THE PROOF COST NOTHING NEW.** An output row became a three-digit index - tile, mma within the tile, row within the mma - which is `MixedRadix.two_digit_unique` verbatim: `warp_row` is its **seventh consumer**. `warp_row_is_a_tile_row` shows the warp tile FACTORS THROUGH the single-mma tiling, so everything already proved about `tile_row` still describes the kernel; the tile loop is `owner` again, so it inherits `GridStrideSplit`'s coverage - **the third axis of this one kernel to do so.** `without_the_tile_guard_a_cta_addresses_past_the_matrix` is what makes the stride guard load-bearing rather than an optimisation: the overrun is PAST THE MATRIX, not a duplicate write.
  - **PROCESS: I RAN TWO ZK SWEEPS CONCURRENTLY AND DISCARDED BOTH.** A chained launch and a relaunch both fired; `ps -eo pid,ppid` showed two independent ROOTS (the innocent case is a subshell whose parent is the other). Both happened to report `138 bad=0` and **both were discarded and re-run serially anyway** - a contended run is not a result, whatever it says. *`pgrep -fc` counts subshells and waiters; check parentage before concluding you have two sweeps, and before concluding you have one.*
  - **PROCESS: my own corpus sweep wrote 55 `.ll` files next to the sources** - the "a gate that emits must run on a COPY" rule, violated in the scratch script written to check the change. Harmless (untracked, and every committed `.ptx` regenerated byte-identically, which is itself the confirmation that the emitter change touched nothing else), and re-run on copies.

Nothing new was needed about the PARTITION - `GridStrideSplit` has had that since the attention kernel - and **ONE licence hypothesis serves both folds, because it bounds the sum of ABSOLUTE values and every partial of either fold is a sum over a SUBSET of the products.** Measured at the licensed maximum K, where every partial of both folds is at its worst, M=16 N=8, every operand 127: **exact at nz = 1, 2, 3, 8, 17 and 64.** 17 is in that sweep deliberately - the theorem has no divisibility precondition and a sweep of powers of two would not say so.

They ARE caught by `coqc`, because `wclass_exact`'s script applies `wrap32_id` and that step stops typechecking - but that is a **PROOF-SCRIPT detail**, the incidental pinning this file already records as too weak to rely on. The deliberate guard is an assertion on the DEFINITIONS' TEXT, added before the sweep for exactly that reason. *The guard belongs on the statement's text* extends to a DEFINITION's text.

One `assert ... by reflexivity` plus a rewrite. So the branch is made VISIBLE and the validator **refuses by name**, pointing at the name-keyed refactor the residue records as a project. A crash in a validator reads as a missing feature; a refusal reads as a work item.
  - **THE SAME COMPREHENSION BUG BIT TWO OF MY OWN GATES.** `liftgap --selftest` and `docgate` both call `ptx_back_edges` bare inside a list comprehension, so a legitimate new refusal became a traceback - and `liftgap --selftest` then reported **rc=0**, because the `$?` I read belonged to `tail` at the end of a pipeline. *A gate that crashes is not a gate that failed, and a pipeline's exit code is the last command's.*
  - **AND A SECOND UNGATED PUBLISHED FIGURE, IN THE GATE I WROTE ONE INCREMENT AGO.** `frontier.check_doc`'s `-O1` branch asserted the sole-blocker SET and nothing else, so the `112 distinct blockers` and `10 clear` it publishes were **checked by nothing** - a gate that asserts the ROUTE and never the NUMBER, which is the certificate-count defect of two increments ago, committed by me, inside the gate written to stop published figures going stale. Both are asserted now. Re-measured: `-O3` **108 -> 109** and `-O1` **112 -> 113**, `10` clear unchanged, and `y_cpu_matmul` still the one kernel one blocker away.
  - **THE SURVIVOR WAS AN UNREACHABLE GUARD, WHICH IS THIS INCREMENT'S OWN SUBJECT ONE LAYER IN.** Removing the SASS multi-section refusal is caught by **nothing**: both corpus modules with two `.text` sections also have two `.entry` points, so the PTX guard refuses first and **no artifact in the corpus can reach the SASS one**. The recorded precedent is to keep it defensive with a comment saying it is not covered; that is the wrong answer in the increment whose finding is *an unreachable check is an untested one*, so `liftgap --selftest` builds a **synthetic two-section disassembly** and requires the refusal, with the one-section direction asserted beside it so "refuse every file" cannot pass. Re-run, it is caught.
  - **PROCESS: MY OWN HARNESS TRUNCATED ITS MEASUREMENT.** `cargo test 2>&1 | tail -200 > file` reported **31 result lines against 147** - which is the exact tell this file records for an ABORTED aggregate, produced here by my own `tail`. The run had completed normally. *The tell is right and it does not distinguish a short run from a short capture; capture everything.*
  - **PROCESS: A BLOCKQUOTE I INSERTED SWALLOWED THE PARAGRAPH AFTER IT.** The doc's lazy-continuation sweep (`awk 'prev ~ /^>/ && $0 !~ /^>/ && NF > 0'`) caught it, which is the second time that check has paid for itself; and the same pass found `0 of 32` still standing in the README after the doc had moved to 38 - *grep the OLD number after any correction, not only the new one*.
  - **PROCESS: THE ROW RUNNER RESTORES AT THE START OF A ROW, NOT THE END**, so the tree still carried M3 when I went on to edit `liftgap.py` - and the new control fired on the correct-looking tree, which reads exactly like a broken control. It was the control working. *Before debugging a control that fires, check whether the last probe is still applied.*
  - **MUTATION TABLE, 16 rows, 14 probes, five checks (`regress.sh`, `fpgate.py`, `docgate.py`, `liftgap.py --selftest`, `frontier.py --selftest`), each run separately.** **M0 CONTROL, two entries of the self-check's fixture list reordered: green everywhere** - read first. **BASE green at the TOP and again at the BOTTOM** - read second, and the closing one is what says no row contaminated the tree. **M1b THE FAITHFUL PRE-INCREMENT STATE (regex back to `%p(\d+)`, guard index back to `int()`, the named-predicate refusal gone, the self-check neutered) / M2 the scanner stops at the first inner brace again: `docgate` + `liftgap` ONLY**, with **all 16 standing results, `fpgate` and the frontier's own controls green** - which is what says the defect was invisible to everything that ships. **M3 the SASS multi-section refusal removed / M5 the predicated back edge not counted / M6 the named predicate not counted / M10 `ptxexec`'s own refusal removed: `liftgap` ONLY**, all four. **M5b the COMPOUND (neither new blocker counted): `docgate` + `liftgap`** - each alone leaves the other firing, so the census answer stays 0 and the doc cannot see it; only together do they restore the optimistic `6 of 38`. **M8 `docgate`'s control back to the bare call / M9 the doc census figure stale / M11 the README's copy stale: `docgate` ONLY.** **M1 the regex alone, M4 `ptx_pred_index` accepting any name, and M7 OVER-REFUSAL (every branch unplaceable): every check fails** - the first two at IMPORT, by the self-check's design, and the third is the control that stops "refuse everything" satisfying every assertion about a refusal.
    - **M1 IS NOT THE FAITHFUL REVERT AND SAYING SO IS THE POINT.** Reverting the regex alone leaves `ptx_pred_index` receiving bare digits, so every kernel is refused and the program is merely INCONSISTENT rather than restored. I recorded it as a catch before noticing. **M1b is the row that means something**, and it is the one that shows the original state passes `regress.sh`.

The recorded precedent is to keep such a guard defensive with a comment saying it is uncovered - **the wrong answer in the increment whose finding is that an unreachable check is an untested one**. `liftgap --selftest` builds a SYNTHETIC two-entry module and a SYNTHETIC two-section disassembly and requires both refusals, with the single-entry and single-section directions asserted beside them so "refuse every file" cannot pass. Re-run, both are caught.
