Measured: **the three nearest kernels are all `UNROLLED x4`** (`exact_pv`, `naive_gemm_f32`, `y_cpu_matmul`, each at distance 3), so every one of them has an uncounted blocker behind it. (b) **`unroll.py` is not fit to be crossed in yet**: it gives a verdict for **18 of 66** (23 `nan`, 24 no row), it RESTATES both back-edge finders rather than importing `loopcfg`, and it pairs PTX loop 0 with SASS loop 0 - which is how `bn254_fr_mul` reports an "unroll factor" of **55** from 6 PTX loops against 1 SASS loop. (c) The six coprocessor kernels are now correctly reported as two SEQUENTIAL loops each and remain blocked on the **name-keyed register file** in `ptxexec`, which is a refactor with its own table. (d) `cvt.rn.f16.f32` is still the highest-reach unmodelled opcode at 7, sole blocker of nothing. (e) `FMUL` and `FMIN` commutativity stay deliberately unassumed. (f) **923 of the 925 emitted `mma.sync` are floating point and carry no proof of any kind.**


**THE DIRECTIVE CENSUS: which `@`-directives are implemented once and ignored everywhere else.** After finding `@ZeroDrift` diverging between two backends and absent from a third, the generalisation is to ask it of every directive rather than wait to trip over the next one. The lexer knows 25; screening each for consumers outside `lexer.rs`/`parser.rs`/`ast.rs` produced four with none.
  - **`@inline`, `@noinline`, `@avx_emit` are LEXED and never PARSED** — dedicated `TokenKind`s that no parser arm matches. Writing one is `Line 1: Error: Unexpected top-level item`, i.e. fail-closed with an unhelpful message. Safe, and worth knowing: the lexer advertises three features the language does not have.
  - **`@gpu_uncached` / `@atomic` / `@align` on a struct field ARE parsed**, into `FieldAttr`, and are read by `llvm_emitter` (volatile, atomic ordering, alignment) and by `c_emitter` — **which is the orphan file that is not compiled**. `ptx_emitter` reads field attributes nowhere. That looked like the `@ZeroDrift` shape again and is not, for a stateable reason: the PTX backend has no struct field access at all, so a field carrying the attribute cannot be read there. Which is how the actual bug turned up.
  - **`@static_assert` is consumed** (`StaticAssertDecl` → `CompileTimeAssert`, 18 references). Not a gap; the raw-name screen under-reports whenever the AST renames a directive, so every hit has to be chased to its AST type before it counts.

**`Expr::MemberAccess` was the LAST arm in `ptx_emitter::emit_expr` still falling through to `""`.** Found by chasing the census above. `x.lane` in an argument position emitted `cvt.rn.f32.s32 %f1, ;` — a comma with nothing after it — under "Compilation Successful!" and exit 0, with `ptxas` rejecting the file afterwards, on whatever machine tries to run it. The hole was closed for `Expr::Ident`, for `Expr::BoolLit` and for the `_` arm in earlier sessions and never for this one: **enumerate the SITES, not the variants**, for the fourth time.
  - **The durable part is a structural gate, not the fix: `no_emitted_instruction_has_a_missing_operand`.** Every bug of this shape — `Expr::Ident`, the `_` arm, `mbarrier_*`, `mma_sync`, `MemberAccess` — produces the same artifact signature, `, ;` or `, ,`. Checking the SIGNATURE catches the next one without anyone guessing which arm it will be in. **Verified live by planting a bad `.ptx` in `tests/` and watching it fail**, not by assuming — a sweep that finds nothing reports "no missing operands" perfectly.
  - The control is what stops "refuse all member access": `.x/.y/.z/.w` on a v4 load is how every eight-limb BN254 kernel in this repo is written, and deleting that branch fails two tests. Mutation-verified 3/3.
  - **The corpus is the evidence the fix is safe**: `--emit-ptx` over `tests/*.ysu` is **59 compile / 26 refuse before AND after**, byte-identical file lists. Take the baseline before the change, not after.
  - **AND THE REFUSAL BASELINE WAS READ, which is the rule this repo already wrote down and had not applied here.** All 26: twenty-four are "this source declares no `kernel`" (host programs and `coprocessor_*.ysu`, correctly fail-closed), one is the type checker refusing a raw dereference in a `@safe` block, and `train_spec.ysu` is a **cascade** — `@ZeroDrift` on a bare `F32` with no `@bounds` is correctly refused, after which `acc` is never bound and reads as "the undefined name `acc`". The first message is right and actionable; the second is noise from the first. Nothing unexamined.

**AND THE HOST BACKEND IGNORED IT ENTIRELY — the `@ZeroDrift`-does-nothing era was still running in `--emit-cpu`.** `cpu_emitter.rs` contains **zero** references to `zero_drift`, and it did not refuse: given a `@ZeroDrift @bounds(-1024, 1024) let mut acc: F32`, it printed `let mut acc = 0.0; acc += 0.1;` and **exited 0**, while `--emit-llvm` on the identical source reported `@ZeroDrift acc: F32 -> Q32.32 (measured 1922 ps/acc)` and lowered it exactly. A plain float reduction is precisely the thing the directive forbids.
  - **Worse than an ordinary unhandled construct, because `--emit-cpu` prints Rust for the user to PASTE.** Y never compiles that output, so nothing downstream ever gets a chance to object — the guarantee is dropped somewhere between the source and a file on someone's clipboard. Refused by name now, pointing at `--emit-llvm`.
  - **`--emit-native` refuses too, but INCIDENTALLY** — floats, `for`, and `=` are all outside its straight-line integer subset, so a drift accumulator cannot be written for it at all. Recorded as a weak pass rather than as coverage: it has no drift path either, and if it ever grows one it must grow a decision with it.
  - **The generalisable assertion is a census, not a per-backend list: no backend may ACCEPT a `@ZeroDrift` program without saying something about the directive.** Honouring it (print the representation selected) and refusing it are both fine; exiting 0 in silence is not. Written as a sweep so a backend added later is covered without anyone remembering to come back, with a non-vacuity floor because a census in which every backend refuses asserts nothing.
  - **Mutation-verified 2/3 caught, 1 survivor sorted.** Making the refusal arm emit the accumulator anyway — a warning rather than a refusal — leaves everything green, because `main.rs` checks `emit_errors` and `exit(1)`s at line 1645 *before* it prints the blob at 1649. So that assertion is a claim about the CLI, which is the layer that decides what reaches the clipboard, and **not** about `cpu_emitter`; the test says so rather than being read as covering the arm.

**`@ZeroDrift` MEANT TWO DIFFERENT THINGS IN THE TWO BACKENDS, and the gotcha-applies-to-every-backend rule found it for the fourth time (`tests/zero_drift_backend_agreement.rs`).** Phase 0 fixed `acc = acc + e` in `llvm_emitter` (it was `store double` into an `alloca i64`). **The PTX backend had the identical hole and nobody looked.** It has a drift arm for `Stmt::CompoundAssign` and had none for `Stmt::Assign`, so the running-sum spelling — which is how the recognised GEMM nest is written — fell through to the ordinary assignment path and emitted `cvt.rn.f64.s64` / `cvt.rn.f32.f64` / `add.f32` / `cvt.rzi.u64.f32` under `// [Y ZERO DRIFT] sum: I64 accumulated exactly as I64`. Three wrongs at once: the accumulation is f32 so everything above 2^24 rounds, the write-back is **unsigned** on a sum that is routinely negative, and the whole round trip is pointless for a representation that already holds the integer. It assembles and it launches.
  - **A SECOND, independent defect was underneath it and hit the WORKING path too**: `emit_drift_from_fixed` narrowed `s64 → f64 → f32` unconditionally, so every read of an exact `I64` accumulator lost the top 40 bits even under `+=`. Its own doc comment said "Converts a fixed-point accumulator back to an `f32` register" — the design assumed the accumulator always encodes a float, which is the contract for a Q format and not for an exact integer one. `emit_drift_to_fixed` had the mirror version, round-tripping every added term through `f64`.
  - **The rule now lives in `zero_drift::running_sum` and BOTH backends call it.** "Which assignments preserve drift-freedom" is a fact about the language, not about a target, and a second copy is how the two came to disagree. `acc = e + acc` is deliberately still refused even though addition commutes — recognising it means deciding per operator whether the accumulator may sit on the right, and the refusal already names `+=` as the one-character repair.
  - **The load-bearing test needs no knowledge of what correct PTX looks like: the two spellings must emit BYTE-IDENTICAL kernels.** Paired with a positive assertion, because an equality test is satisfied by two kernels that are identically wrong. The positive one is *not* a banned-opcode list — the first version was, and it MISSED `cvt.rn.f64.s64`. The right assertion is that **this program contains no float at all**, so no instruction in it may mention one.
  - **Mutation-verified 6/6 caught, 1 survivor sorted.** Reverting the accumulator's register type to untyped (`alloc_reg64`, i.e. the `%rd`→U64 default that produced the unsigned write-back) **passes everything**, because the new arms write `add.s64` literally and never consult `ty_of(acc)`. Kept as defensive, with the comment saying it is not covered — the generic path that DOES read it is one deleted guard away. Note also that dropping the `Assign` arm alone no longer reproduces the float accumulation, because the `from_fixed` fix independently repairs the arithmetic; the byte-identity test is what catches that mutation.
  - **Found by running every backend over the newest source in the repo.** The Phase 0 exact-GEMM nest did not exist when the empty-artifact sweep ran. Four backends refuse it correctly by name (`--emit-cpu`, `--emit-native`, `--emit-coprocessor`, and `--target=r1cs`); `--emit-ptx` accepted it and emitted the wrong arithmetic. **A backend sweep is not a one-time act — re-run it against each new source shape.**
  - `tests/test_drift.ptx` is the only committed artifact affected and the diff is cosmetic (`mov.u64` → `mov.s64` on a bit-copy), because the fixed-point path was already correct. Regenerated anyway: a fixed producer does not fix what it already wrote.

**PHASE 1'S SECOND THEOREM IS THE OUTPUT TILING, AND WRITING IT FOUND A LIVE OUT-OF-BOUNDS HEAP WRITE (`proofs/ExactGemmTiling.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_tiling_model.rs`).** The K-split is a REDUCTION - the bands are summed, so the obligation is that they tile the range. The output tiling is a PARTITION - each `MR x NR` tile writes a disjoint rectangle of C, so the obligation is that every element is written **exactly once**, which a coverage count does not give (a tiling that writes one element twice and another never has exactly the right total width). `tiles_cover`, `tile_index_injective`, `tile_index_surjective`, `c_written_exactly_once`; Rocq 9.1, no axioms.
  - **The theorem needs `N <= ldc`, and nothing in the compiler states it.** With a shorter row stride two distinct `(row, col)` pairs collapse onto one address (`row_stride_below_n_aliases`). Every caller passes `ldc = N`, so nothing had ever called the exact kernel with a padded C.
  - **Doing so found THREE sites in `emit_vnni_threaded_module` treating C as contiguous `M*N`.** (a) `memset(C, 0, M*N*8)` zeroes into early rows' padding and leaves the **last rows' live cells unzeroed** - and the kernel ACCUMULATES, so that is a wrong answer, not cosmetic; (b) the worker's job slot 8 stored the caller's `%ldc` while its private C is a compact `M*N` buffer, so a worker wrote `(M-1)*(ldc-N)` elements past the end - **heap overflow, observed as `double free or corruption`**; (c) the reduction walked source and destination with one flat index, correct only when the strides are equal. All three fixed; verified at 1/2/4/8 threads with `lda = K+5`, `ldb = N+9`, `ldc = N+7` and both axes ragged.
  - **THE DISCRIMINATING EXPERIMENT CAME BEFORE THE DIAGNOSIS.** A heap corruption in a test I had just written is as likely to be my driver's bug as the kernel's. Re-running the identical driver with `lda = K, ldb = N, ldc = N` gives `wrong 0 clobbered 0`; then varying one stride at a time isolated `ldc`; then varying the thread count split the single root cause into its two symptoms (1 thread: right answer, 336 clobbered padding cells; >=2 threads: heap corruption). Four cheap runs, and each one removed an explanation.
  - **This is exactly the class §1 of `docs/proof_carrying_kernels.md` cites** - "twelve address computations in the CPU GEMM were correct only because `lda == K` made stride and extent the same number" - found again, in the exact kernel, by the programme that exists because of it. **Make every stride differ from its extent in any GEMM test; equality is a coincidence that hides address bugs.**
  - **The honest causal story: the proof did not find the bug, and that version is more interesting.** Formalising forced the `N <= ldc` hypothesis to be STATED; stating it suggested the test; the test found the bug. A proof's value here was surfacing an unwritten precondition, not discharging it.
  - **The behavioural tie is stronger than the K-split's, and for a stateable reason.** A correct K-split is invisible in the answer - that is what `ksplit_exact` says - so that model could only predict a thread count. A tile that overruns writes MEMORY IT DOES NOT OWN, which a padded, poisoned C observes directly. **And the driver must NOT pre-zero the live region**: the wrapper owns that zeroing, and pre-zeroing masks exactly half the bug (the unzeroed-tail half). My first version did pre-zero and reported `wrong 0`.
  - Mutation-verified 8/8: the three fixed sites, the Rust transcription unclamped, the transcription dropping its final partial tile, the emitter's own clamp, and two hypotheses of the proof (the tile-width clamp and `N <= ldc`) - the last two caught because the file then fails to compile.
  - **A test whose assertion is a guess at emitted syntax is a test of the guess.** `the_model_and_the_driver_agree_on_the_tile_shape` first looked for `llvm.smin`, which the IR builder does not emit - it builds `icmp slt` + `select`. It matches the real instruction now.

**PHASE 1 HAS ITS FIRST THEOREM: the exact GEMM's K-SPLIT SCHEDULE (`proofs/ExactGemmKsplit.v`).** Phase 0 left "bit-identical at every thread count" as a property six thread counts at one shape happen to exhibit. `bands_tile` proves the emitted decomposition (`base = K/nthr`, `rem = K%nthr`, first `rem` bands one longer) covers `[0, K)` exactly for every K and every positive nthr; `ksplit_exact` proves the per-band partials sum to the naive sum, with **no** hypothesis that K divides evenly or that the bands are equal; `any_thread_count_agrees` is the property `tests/exact_gemm_thread_invariance.rs` asserts, **derived** — and it says nothing about threads, because two counts agree by each separately equalling the naive nest. Rocq 9.1, no axioms, nothing admitted.
  - **Section 2's central claim is machine-checked now instead of asserted.** `rounding_breaks_the_split` and `exact_survives_the_same_split` are the SAME f, the same K=201 and the same nthr=2, differing only in the accumulate. The rounded one answers **1100 against its own reference's 1000** — it does not lose precision, it DISAGREES, and no tolerance makes that a proof of anything; the exact one answers 1200 either way. A control pins that the two accumulates really do differ on that input, so the exact case is not passing because the rounding is inert. **Finding the fixture took a brute-force search**: three plausible rounding models (`m*floor(x/m)` for m=2,4,8) turned out to AGREE on every small input tried, so "obviously non-associative" was not enough — the counterexample needs a large term the small ones vanish against, which is the textbook shape and had to be constructed deliberately.
  - **What is deliberately NOT proved is most of the kernel, and the file says so.** A band's partial is MODELLED as the exact sum over its indices, so packing, the 2-D register tile, the masked tails and the int32→int64 flush are assumed rather than verified. Also: accumulators are `Z`, so nothing here says a partial fits in int32 between flushes — that is the licence obligation, discharged EXHAUSTIVELY over the finite int16 domain in `tests/exact_gemm_licence_obligations.rs`. A proof over `Z` plus an exhaustive check over the finite domain is stronger than either alone, and only because both are present.
  - **The model-to-code gap is narrowed in ONE named place rather than waved at.** `cpu_gemm::ksplit_bands` / `ksplit_threads` transcribe the same definitions with the emitted LLVM quoted beside them; `tests/exact_gemm_ksplit_model.rs` checks the transcription against the theorem over 192,000 cases, re-runs the dropped-remainder refutation in Rust (without which the tiling sweep is not obviously testing anything), and asserts the model and the emitter **AGREE** on their constants rather than keeping a third copy. The behavioural tie is `the_min_band_floor_is_what_the_model_says`: sweep K across the min-band floor with the thread request FIXED, and assert the observed `pthread_create` count is `ksplit_threads`'s answer. **A correct band decomposition is invisible in the answer** — that is what the theorem says — so the thread count is the only thing the model predicts that the running code reveals. Mutating either side alone fails it, checked separately in both directions.
  - **A correctness test at one shape does not cover a schedule.** Mutating the emitter's uneven split to an even one (`icmp slt` → `sle`) is caught by the new floor sweep at K=256 and **PASSES** the pre-existing K=4099 invariance test. 8/8 mutations caught overall.
  - **`cargo test` aborts the remaining test binaries after one fails**, so a mutation run that lists several `--test` targets can silently leave the important one unmeasured. M4 looked like it was caught by the pure-model test only; re-run alone, the real-thread sweep catches it too. Re-run each target separately before recording which test caught what.

**THE OTHER KERNEL IN THE SAME FILE HAD THE OPPOSITE LAUNCH CONTRACT, AND NOTHING SAID SO.** Continuing the schedule sweep found a live bug: `attn_accum` is grid-stride and launch-invariant (the module's headline claim), while **`attn_scores` was ONE THREAD PER KEY with a bounds guard and no loop**, silently requiring `gridDim.x * blockDim.x >= S`. Measured on the card at S=512: **128 threads left 768 of 1024 score slots stale and computed the maximum as 34647 against 34752**; 32 threads left 960 stale. **The stale scores are the LESSER half** - `attn_accum` subtracts that maximum from every score, so a wrong one moves *every* softmax weight. Same class as the paged-decode launch contract this file records, and worse: there it is at least written down. Fixed by making it grid-stride - the same residue-class partition `proofs/GridStrideSplit.v` already proves, so the theorem covers it with **no new proof** and the family's contract is uniform. (`&Q[b][0]` moves inside the loop; the inner dot product walks that pointer.) 615 / 881 tests, both builds green.
  - **WHAT COULD NOT SEE IT.** `ptx_portability` runs real `ptxas` at five architectures and passes either way - this repo's own recorded limit, *an assemble gate cannot see a missing instruction*, and here the missing instruction is a whole loop. `exact_attention_bounds` passes too.
  - **THE EXISTING INVARIANCE TEST COULD NOT SEE IT EITHER, AND THE REASON GENERALISES: it sweeps the geometry of `attn_accum` while launching `attn_scores` at ONE FIXED, CORRECT geometry.** A test that sweeps one kernel's launch geometry is not testing the other kernel's. The new test poisons `Scores` with `0xAB` rather than zeroing it - zeroing hides a skipped key behind a plausible value - and asserts every SHORT geometry agrees with a covering one.
  - **THE GATE WAS HARDCODING A RULE THAT HELD FOR TWO OF THREE KERNELS.** It asserted `nworkers` is the product of THREE extents; `attn_scores` mixes only two hardware dimensions. Now DERIVED per kernel: take the hardware indices `worker` actually depends on, map each to its extent (`%ctaid.x` -> `%nctaid.x`), require `nworkers` to be the product of exactly those - fewer and the classes overlap, more and they stop covering.
  - **A STRUCTURAL PATTERN MATCHED MORE THAN ONE THING FOR THE THIRD TIME IN THIS FILE.** "The stride update is `add.s32 %X, %X, %rY` after the marker" also matches `add.s32 %r12, %r12, %r4`, an ordinary `b*S + i` flat-index computation, so the loop counter came out as address arithmetic. Anchored on the loop's **back-edge** now - the increment is the last such instruction before the branch closing the loop, a property of loops rather than a shape that is unique today. First the marker, now the back-edge: **both times the fix was to anchor on something the kernel actually SAYS.**
  - **THE LAST PRECONDITION IS REMOVED, AND THE MUTATION THAT SURVIVED IS THE FINDING.** `red.global.max` needs no order argument (max is associative, commutative AND idempotent, which `GridStrideSplit.v` covers), but its IDENTITY came from the host: a signed max wants `i32::MIN`, not a uniform byte pattern, so `M` could not take the `memset(0)` that L, O and P take. A caller who used one anyway was wrong **only when a row's scores were all negative** - which cannot happen on random int8 data, so every test passed either way. **That is the worst shape a precondition can have.** Fixed by biasing into unsigned space (`x ^ 0x80000000`, the order-preserving signed->unsigned bijection): unsigned max has identity **0**, so a zeroed buffer MEANS `i32::MIN` and the module's contract is uniform. The two accumulating entries undo the bias on load.
    - **DELETING THE UNDO FROM ONE OF THE TWO ACCUMULATING ENTRIES PASSED EVERYTHING, INCLUDING THE ACCUM-VS-NAIVE DIFFERENTIAL ON `p`** - the comparison that exists to catch exactly a one-sided change. The exp argument is `((m - s) * KFix + 2^15) >> 16` computed in 64 bits and then **truncated to u32**, so a missing undo shifts it by `2^15 * KFix`, and every test passed `KFix = 8 << 16 = 2^19`, for which that is `2^34` - **exactly zero modulo 2^32**. The truncation annihilated the bug at the one temperature every arm shared. `feedback-differential-arms-share-constants` in an unfamiliar place: not a factor both sides multiply by, but a constant that makes a WRONG value truncate to the right one. A real model's `q_scale * k_scale / sqrt(d)` does not oblige.
    - `the_accumulating_entries_undo_the_bias` uses `2^19 + 1` (the same temperature to within 2e-6, odd, so the shift is `2^15` and a missing undo drives almost every weight to zero) and checks `p` against `fixed_exp::exp2_neg_q16_16` on the host over the device's own scores. **That is the oracle `p` never had**: the existing test's docstring says `p` is "a per-element function of `s`, so it is not what is in question here" - true of the REDUCTION claim, and the undo lives exactly there. **When a docstring explains why something is out of scope, check what has since moved into it.**
    - `a_zeroed_max_buffer_is_the_identity` is the other half: an all-negative-score fixture (Q strictly positive, K strictly negative) seeded with a plain `memset(0)`, with a non-vacuity assertion that the true maximum really is negative - the case only bites there, and a fixture that drifted positive would pass while asserting nothing.
    - Six mutations, all caught, and `gpu_attention_invariance` is the only suite that fires for any of them: full revert to a signed max; drop the bias in `attn_scores` only; drop the undo in each accumulating entry separately; bias with `0x40000000` (not order-preserving); keep the bias but reduce with a SIGNED max. 617 / 883 tests, both builds green.
    - A stale exclusion went with it: `every_reducing_entry_was_actually_examined`'s docstring still said `attn_scores` "is deliberately excluded - it is one thread per key and reduces nothing". That exclusion WAS the bug, and the comment outlived the fix by one commit.
  - **THE SWEEP FOR THE SAME CLASS FOUND THE SATURATE, ONE LINE DOWN.** `min.s64 %rd50, %rd50, 1073741824` sits between the `shr.s64` and the `cvt.u32.u64`. Without it a large score delta wraps modulo 2^32 at the narrowing and a **far** key comes back with a **small** argument - a weight near 2^28, i.e. the weight of the BEST key. Not precision loss: attention paid to the wrong token.
    - **Deleting it from the emitter passes `gpu_attention_invariance` on a real card.** At head_dim 32 and C = 2^-13 the argument never approaches 2^32, so no device fixture can reach it. The parameters that DO are ones this repo already sweeps: `C = 3.0e-2` is the largest scale in `the_temperature_multiplier_carries_two_to_the_thirty_two`'s own list and head_dim 128 is a shape `the_shapes_a_model_uses_still_generate` generates. There, a key **2,184,534 below the maximum** comes back at 0.986 x 2^28.
    - **What was missing is the NECESSITY, not the presence.** The literal was already pinned by a substring assertion, so removing or moving it failed - but a check that a line exists says nothing about what happens without it. And the host replica in the temperature test is `((ds * kfix + 32768) >> 16) as f64`, with no clamp and **no narrowing**: both conventions it exists to separate live ABOVE the point where the guard acts, so it is right about the multiplier and silent about everything else. **Nothing anywhere modelled the u32.**
    - `the_saturate_is_what_stops_a_far_key_wrapping_into_a_large_weight` models the arithmetic ONCE with the guard as a parameter (so the two readings cannot drift), SEARCHES for the wrapping delta rather than hardcoding it, carries the control that stops `min(t, 0)` passing (in range the guard must be a no-op), shows the value is the exp's own saturation point, and ties the model to the emitter. Four mutations caught: remove the guard, clamp at 2^31, clamp after the narrowing, and drop the clamp from BOTH arms of the model - the vacuous-necessity case. 618 / 884 tests, both builds green.

**THE CERTIFICATE IS EMITTED NOW, AND TWO OF SEVEN MUTATIONS SURVIVED FOR ONE REASON (`src/exact_gemm_certificate.rs`, `tests/exact_gemm_certificate.rs`).** `proofs/` is checked once at build time against the shipped schedule; its theorems quantify over `M`, `N`, `K` and `nthr`, so every shape is covered - and a user compiling their own `@ZeroDrift` nest got a fast kernel and **no artifact**. "Proof-carrying" described the repository, not the output. `--emit-llvm` now writes `<stem>_certificate.v` beside the `.ll` whenever the exact `vpdpwssd` kernel is SUBSTITUTED, **instantiating** `ExactGemmWhole.the_threaded_gemm_holds_the_source_dot_products` at this compilation's flush interval and operand bound rather than re-proving anything. `Y_NO_CERTIFICATE=1` suppresses it, loudly. 633 / 899 tests, both builds green.
  - **IT IS NOT PAPERWORK, AND THE REASON IS THAT TWO TOOLS DERIVE ONE OBLIGATION.** The only hypothesis depending on the program is the LICENCE. Y decides it in **floating point** - a `sqrt` and a `floor` on `f64` in `VnniExact::max_operand_magnitude`. The certificate states `2 * Fl * m^2 <= i32::MAX` over `Z` and hands it to `coqc`, which has no floats. Verified at the edge BEFORE anything was wired in: at the default interval the certificate is **accepted at `m = 4095` and refused at `m = 4096`** - the same one-unit boundary `tests/exact_gemm_licence_obligations.rs` finds by exhausting int16, reproduced by a different tool from a different derivation. `the_certificate_refuses_exactly_the_bounds_the_compiler_refuses` runs the comparison at four intervals, at the limit and one above.
  - **`m` PLAYS TWO ROLES AND `ceil` IS CONSERVATIVE FOR BOTH.** The licence gets HARDER as `m` grows; the data hypothesis `|A[i,k]| <= m` gets EASIER. So `floor` would be wrong twice - licensing against a smaller bound than the source declared AND leaving the operands between `floor(m)` and `m` uncovered while the kernel consumes them. It cannot break a licence Y granted (`m <= L` with `L` integral gives `ceil(m) <= L`), and that is checked over every admissible interval rather than argued. **Only a FRACTIONAL `@bounds` makes the direction observable** - every other fixture declares an integer bound where the two agree.
  - **8 mutations, 8 caught after the two survivors below were closed. SURVIVOR 1: the licence statement with one factor of `m` dropped passes all seven tests, including the coqc sweep.** **Coq compares propositions up to CONVERSION**: at a licensed numeral both `2*Fl*m <= I32MAX` and `2*Fl*m*m <= I32MAX` reduce to `Lt <> Gt`, so the wrong statement type-checks AND its use site - which still demands the real hypothesis - accepts it by conversion too. The mutated certificate refuses **exactly** the magnitudes the correct one refuses; no `coqc` run can separate them. What changes is the claim a human auditing the artifact reads, which for a certificate is the whole point of the artifact.
  - **SURVIVOR 2: `Theorem the_certificate_is_not_vacuous : True.` also passes** - it compiles, reports `Closed under the global context`, and satisfies a COUNT of how many such reports appeared. Same lesson: **`coqc` accepting a generated proof is necessary and not sufficient**, and the guard belongs on the statement's TEXT. That is `every_proof_has_a_content_control` in `tests/proofs_are_checked.rs`, which guards the COMMITTED proofs against precisely this and had no counterpart for the GENERATED one. Both are closed by asserting the certificate states the obligation it is about and evaluates the model it claims to.
  - **The file name is sanitised in `main.rs`, not only in the renderer.** `coqc` derives the module's logical name from the FILE name, so sanitising one side alone leaves a certificate whose own "check with" line names a module that does not exist. `4-bit gemm.ysu` is an ordinary source name and an illegal Coq identifier.
  - **The controls are what stop "always write a certificate" passing.** A nest with no operand `@bounds` is still EXACT - scalar lowering honours `@ZeroDrift` - it is simply not licensed for the fast kernel, and then there is nothing to certify because the emitted code IS the naive nest. No certificate for that, none under `Y_NO_GEMM_RECOGNISER=1`, both asserted.
  - **A gate that runs `coqc` must build the library ONCE per directory.** The first licence sweep rebuilt all fourteen proofs for each of its eight probes: 117s for zero additional coverage, 19.5s after splitting `coq_prepare` from `coqc`.
  - **A transient 4-failure run was NOT the mutation and chasing it cost twenty minutes.** Under a mid-rebuild binary the suite reported four NotFound failures that never reproduced; running the same mutation cleanly gave a green suite, which was the real (and more interesting) result. **Verify the mutated artifact actually contains the mutation before reading any suite result** - `grep` the generated file, not the source.

**`--emit-cpu` CLAIMED AVX IN SIX PLACES AND EMITS NO SIMD ANYWHERE (`src/main.rs`, `src/cpu_emitter.rs`, `src/avx_wrapper.rs` DELETED, `tests/emit_cpu_claims_no_simd.rs`).** The residue recorded one entry down - `avx_wrapper` referenced by nothing, 556 lines, four passing tests - was not merely dead: it was **the thing that made the word "AVX" look backed** everywhere it appeared. **576 / 827 / 8 tests, zero failures across 131 per-target binaries in both feature sets plus all three aggregates; both builds warning-free; corpus unchanged at 46 accept / 39 refuse; no committed `.ptx`/`.ll`/`.v` changed. The totals are UNCHANGED from the previous increment and the arithmetic closes exactly: +4 integration tests, -4 deleted `avx_wrapper` unit tests.**
  - **THE CENSUS: CLI banner `Emitting CPU AVX-512 Host Code...`; blob marker `======= GENERATED RUST/AVX BLOB =======`; README flag table "prints Rust/AVX source"; language reference flag table "Host Rust/AVX source"; language reference §9.7 documenting an `@avx_emit` directive; and `docs/proof_carrying_kernels.md`'s Phase 0 paragraph, "a shape dispatcher ... that emits hand-written Rust/AVX".** Measured over the whole corpus: **46 blobs emitted, 0 containing a vector intrinsic, a vector type, an `x86_64::` path or a `target_feature` attribute**, and `_mm256`/`_mm512` appear **zero** times in `cpu_emitter.rs`. The `@zk_target(scheme = "plonkish")` shape - an artifact naming a capability it did not use - and **fail-loud in NO direction**, which is why six copies accumulated: each was written by someone reading one of the others.
  - **THE SHAPE DISPATCHER THE ROADMAP CITED IS UNREACHABLE.** `emit_specialized_cpu_kernel_dispatch` - `CpuShapeDispatcher`, `classify_shape`, all five `CpuMatrixRegime` variants and all five `emit_*_kernel` methods - has **exactly ONE caller in the repository and it is a test**. No `.ysu` compilation reaches it, so `--emit-cpu` does not have GEMM kernels that happen to be scalar, it has **no GEMM kernels at all**. Same shape as `run_all_optimization_passes`. **This also corrects the previous increment**, which called `probe_cpu_hardware_profile`'s consumer "a performance fallback, not a correctness one" - true, and understated: no compilation reaches it.
  - **THE DEAD MODULE CONTAINED REAL DEFECTS, WHICH IS THE WHOLE REASON TO AUDIT BEFORE DELETING.** (a) `Y256f32::load_aligned_ptr(src: *const f32)` and `store_aligned_ptr` are **safe `pub fn`s that dereference a raw pointer** - they assert non-null and 32-byte alignment, neither of which establishes validity or that eight floats are readable, and a safe function must not permit UB. (b) The **entire AVX2 surface** calls `_mm256_*` with **no `#[target_feature]` and no runtime guard**, while `require_avx2()` - doc comment *"Call once at start-up. Panics if AVX2 is unavailable"* - has **zero callers**, so the module's documented safety protocol was never enforced. Identical shape to `Y512f32`'s "Only constructed if `has_avx512f()` returns true" with `has_avx512f()` also at zero callers. **Four passing tests made all of it look maintained: a dead module WITH TESTS is worse than a dead module.**
  - **§9.7 NOW STATES WHAT WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN WHAT WAS INTENDED, and the three directives do not even fail alike**: **`@avx_emit` is a hard syntax error** (`Line 1: Error: Unexpected top-level item`), while **`@ptx_emit` and `@hdl_emit` parse, are ignored, and exit 0** - the worse direction, since a user selecting a backend gets a clean compile and no sign the annotation was discarded. (The `@ptx_emit`/`@hdl_emit` no-op is RECORDED, not fixed - it is the `plonkish` shape and wants its own increment.)
  - **PHASE 0'S "BOTH BACKENDS" CLAUSE IS DROPPED, NOT DEFERRED, AND ON EVIDENCE.** That clause told a future reader to "re-scope it deliberately or drop it". Its premise was false twice over: there is no second GEMM in `--emit-cpu` to be exact in, because the dispatcher is unreachable and what is emitted is scalar. **The clause was not hard, it was EMPTY.** Phase 0's exactness result stands on the LLVM backend alone, stated so nobody reads a single-backend result as a shortfall against a clause that measured nothing.
  - **THE GATE IS NECESSARILY HALF SOURCE-LEVEL, and pairing the two halves is the design.** Whether the compiler PRINTS an AVX claim is a property of a string literal - running it on a machine where it emits scalar code says nothing about the banner - so that half is pinned at the source, the same device as pinning which CPUID reading a predicate uses. The other half is the structural fact the claim is *about*: no emitted blob may contain SIMD, swept over the corpus with a floor counting blobs **scanned**. Neither suffices: the source gate alone permits an emitter that grows SIMD while the docs stay silent; the corpus gate alone permits the docs to keep advertising what is not there.
  - **WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED**: whether a reader's `rustc` auto-vectorizes the emitted scalar loops. **Two attempts to measure it produced NULLS** - once the crate-type emitted no code for an unused function (a 3-line `.s` file), once the symbol was eliminated - and the honest framing is that this is a property of the reader's compiler, not of what Y emits. "Source that some compiler may vectorize" describes all source. **State the claim you can hold and record the one you dropped.**
  - **MUTATION TABLE, 8 probes, each `--test` target run separately over nine suites.** **C1 the banner claims AVX-512 again / C3 the README row claims Rust/AVX again / C4 §9.7 drops "NOT IMPLEMENTED" / C6 the blob sweep neutered with the floor kept: `emit_cpu_claims_no_simd` ONLY, all four** - so **four of the six claim sites were invisible to every other suite**, which is how six copies accumulated. C5 the emitter emits `_mm256_…`: the new gate, two of its tests firing. C2 the marker claims RUST/AVX again, and C8 the backend emits a header and nothing else: the new gate plus both blob harnesses - diagnosis by name rather than isolation, since the harnesses already fail on those, just less legibly. **C7 CONTROL, two entries of the marker list reordered: green everywhere**, read first.
    - **C8 WAS MIS-AIMED ON THE FIRST PASS** (`self.buffer` is not a field) and came back BUILD FAILED. Re-aimed at a return yielding only the header, it is caught. *Confirm a mutation compiles and reproduces the defect before recording anything about it.*
  - **THE CITATION GATE CAUGHT ME, ON A LIVE CASE.** `every_path_a_proof_or_a_gate_cites_exists` failed on the new suite's first run: its module docstring cited `src/avx_wrapper.rs`, which this increment deletes. That is the gate doing exactly its job - *"a docstring pointing at a renamed or deleted file is how a claim about what pins something becomes unfalsifiable"*. The fix is to name the deleted module **without a resolvable path**, and to say in the docstring why, so the next reader does not helpfully restore the citation.

**THE GATE CERTIFIED AN ARTIFACT THE COMPILER DOES NOT EMIT, BECAUSE IT EDITED IT FIRST (`src/cpu_emitter.rs`, `tests/cpu_emitter_output_compiles.rs`, `tests/cpu_emitter_lowering.rs`).** Found by reading the previous increment's own census back as a work queue: it named `avx_wrapper::has_avx512f` as a reading of the AVX-512 question and then dropped it from the gate, and chasing why showed it has **zero callers**. `--emit-cpu` is documented as printing Rust "**for you to paste**" and as "gated on `rustc` accepting what it prints". The first half is true; **the second was false, and the gate is what made that invisible.** **576 / 827 / 8 tests, zero failures across 130 per-target binaries in both feature sets plus all three aggregates; both builds warning-free; corpus unchanged at 46 accept / 39 refuse; no committed `.ptx`/`.ll`/`.v` changed.**
  - **MEASURED: 46 blobs emitted, 46 carry `use crate::avx_wrapper::*;`, ZERO reference a symbol from it.** `crate::` names the Y compiler's own crate and the reader is pasting into theirs, so the artifact this backend exists to produce failed **as delivered, for every program**, with `error[E0432]: unresolved import crate::avx_wrapper` - for a module none of the 46 used.
  - **BOTH HARNESSES THAT COMPILE THE BLOB DELETED THAT LINE BEFORE COMPILING IT.** `cpu_emitter_output_compiles` filtered it with the comment *"the blob is written to be pasted INTO this crate"* - which **contradicts the README one file away**, and the strip is precisely what stopped anyone comparing them. `cpu_emitter_lowering` did the same. Same defect class as the four Python benchmark harnesses that stripped the compiler's PTX header and substituted their own: **a harness that re-wraps the output is measuring something the compiler did not emit** - here in a TEST, which is what licenses the README's claim.
  - **STRIPPING DOES NOT RESCUE IT, IT MOVES THE FAILURE.** As delivered: `E0432` unresolved import. As the gate checked it: `E0433: cannot find type Y256f32`. **The blob did not compile either way**, and the gate passed only because **no corpus program reaches the construct that references `Y256f32`** - so the strip is harmless for the 46 programs the gate sees and blind for the one that needed it. The working path masking the broken one, again.
  - **`Fragment::zero` IS THE FIFTH MEMBER OF A FAMILY THE SWEEP LEFT AT FOUR, ONE MATCH ARM AWAY.** The docstring directly above that arm lists four substitutions refused for *computing something different*, including `ldmatrix(p) -> Y256f32::load_aligned_ptr` - "a warp-cooperative f16 matrix-fragment load rendered as an 8-wide f32 load". `Fragment::zero -> Y256f32::zero` is the same substitution on the same operand type and survived. It was also the blob's ONLY reason to import `crate::avx_wrapper`. Refused now via `unsupported_gpu_intrinsic`, whose message already states the principle: this backend "prints Rust for you to paste, so a plausible-looking substitution would reach your source with no compiler between it and you". **A docstring listing four reads as completeness and is the best available evidence that a fifth was missed - apply the RULE to every sibling arm, not to the cases you thought of.**
  - **SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY: this is fail-LOUD, not silent.** The reader pastes and rustc rejects immediately; nobody ships a wrong answer. What was wrong is a **claim** - "gated on `rustc` accepting what it prints" was true of a modified artifact and false of the emitted one. It is true now.
  - **THE FIX IS WHAT LETS THE GATE CHECK THE ARTIFACT VERBATIM.** Drop the import, refuse `Fragment::zero`, and both harnesses stop stripping - possible only because the blob became self-contained. Corpus unchanged in both directions (46/39 before and after), so the refusal is purely additive. **Fix the PRODUCER so the fixup is unnecessary; do not keep the fixup and document it.** The durable gate is on the defect's SIGNATURE rather than the instance: no emitted blob may contain `use crate::…`, whatever it names, because `crate` is the pasting crate and that is never this one.
    - **AND THE SIGNATURE GATE MUST NOT READ THE EXTRACTOR'S OUTPUT.** Written the obvious way it reads `emit_cpu(..).blob` - and the extractor is **in the same file** and is exactly what hid the defect, so a re-added strip filters the offender out on its way past and the gate reports a clean sweep. It scans the RAW compiler output instead. Established by mutation, and only by a COMPOUND one (see B1+B4).
  - **MUTATION TABLE, 8 probes, each `--test` target run separately over nine suites.** B1 the import restored: both cpu_emitter suites. **B2 `Fragment::zero -> Y256f32::zero` restored: `a_matrix_fragment_has_no_host_equivalent` ONLY.** B3 both restored (the state at HEAD): both cpu_emitter suites. **B1+B4 import restored AND the gate strips again**: both cpu_emitter suites. **B6 the sweep neutered with the floor left in place: the FLOOR only.** B7 over-refusal (refuse every program): 3 suites including the control. **B4 alone (the strip restored, nothing to strip): MIS-AIMED, green.** **B5 CONTROL, two banner `writeln!`s reordered: green everywhere**, read first.
    - **B2 IS THE ISOLATION RESULT AND IT WAS VERIFIED BY NAME RATHER THAN INFERRED**: `no_emitted_blob_is_invalid_rust`, the sweep that compiles all 46 blobs, **passes** under it. No corpus program uses `Fragment::zero`, so the broad sweep is structurally incapable of seeing it and only the named refusal test can. `feedback-exercised-is-not-covered`.
    - **B4 ALONE IS MIS-AIMED AND THAT IS THE HONEST READING**: once the producer is fixed there is no import for a strip to remove, so re-adding the strip reproduces no defect. **The compound is the probe that means something**, and it is what justified reading the raw text - the same shape as the previous increment's A5+A9.
  - **RECORDED, NOT FIXED: `src/avx_wrapper.rs` is now referenced by NOTHING** - 556 lines, four `#[test]`s, and after this change its only mention anywhere is its own `pub mod` line in `lib.rs`. That is the `VnniExact::licenses` shape exactly: **a dead module WITH TESTS, which is worse than a dead module, because the tests are what make it look alive.** Left deliberately - deleting a SIMD abstraction layer is its own increment with its own measurement, and `tests/source_surface.rs`'s rule is satisfied either way since it is a declared module. Named so the next reader need not rediscover it.

**THREE ANSWERS TO "DOES THIS MACHINE HAVE AVX-512", AND THE WRONG ONE FED THE EMITTER - PLUS A FOURTH NOBODY HAD COUNTED (`src/sentinel.rs`, `tests/avx512_probes_agree.rs`).** `probe_cpu_features` reads CPUID leaf 7 EBX[16] with **no `XGETBV` check** and its answer becomes `HardwareProfile::has_avx512` -> `llvm_emitter::host_cpu_attrs` -> the prelude's `attributes #0`, the group the entry below established is applied to EVERY function in the module. `avx_wrapper::has_avx512f` and `sentinel::host_has_avx512` both did the check the emitter's reading did not, and nothing asserted the three agreed. Same shape as `VnniExact::licenses` and the two CUDA driver bindings. **573 / 824 / 8 tests, zero failures across 130 per-target binaries in both feature sets plus all three aggregates; both builds warning-free; all 55 emitted LLVM modules byte-for-byte unchanged; no committed `.ptx`/`.ll`/`.v` changed.**
  - **THERE ARE FOUR PRODUCERS AND THE FOURTH IS THE ONE THAT SHIPS: the CACHED path is not a probe with a gap in it, it is NO PROBE AT ALL.** `check_or_probe_hardware` skips the probe whenever `.ysu_hw_profile` merely exists, so `has_avx512` was whatever the file said. Counting NAMES gives three readings; counting SITES gives four - `enumerate the SITES, not the variants`, for the fifth time in this file.
  - **MEASURED, AND THE TWO ROUTES HAVE OPPOSITE ANSWERS.** Route A (XCR0) is **LATENT here**: `CPUID.7.0:EBX[16]=true`, `XCR0=0x2e7` with all five state bits set, and all four readings answer `true` - they agree **by luck of this machine's configuration, not by construction**. The mechanism was confirmed at the instruction level rather than read off a manual: the std macro's detection path compiles to code containing `xgetbv` and a raw leaf-7 read cannot. Route B (the cached profile) is **REACHABLE RIGHT NOW**, one machine, one binary, the file the only thing varied: `AVX512=true -> target-cpu=znver5 +avx512f,...`; `AVX512=false -> target-cpu=haswell +avx2`. A profile copied from a better machine - or COMMITTED, which has happened here with `SM_VERSION=8.9` - put AVX-512 into every function of the module.
    - An incoherence inside Route B worth its own line: **`host_x86_uarch()` IS probed live** (CPUID vendor+family) while `has_avx512` came from the file, so the two halves of `attributes #0` described two different machines.
  - **THE CACHE REASONING WAS RIGHT ABOUT THE GPU AND WAS SILENTLY EXTENDED TO THE CPU.** The skip comment says nothing here queries the driver "because that would cost every CPU-only compile" - correct for `SM_VERSION`, where validation costs `cuInit`, more than this compiler's entire ZK front end. It does not transfer to CPUID, which is one instruction and no syscall. **Cache the expensive measurement; re-probe the cheap fact**, decided per FIELD rather than inherited from the file as a whole.
  - **THE BLAST RADIUS WAS NARROWER THAN ASSUMED AND SAYING SO IS PART OF THE WORK.** `has_avx512` does NOT feed the analytic cost model. Exhaustively outside `sentinel.rs`: `llvm_emitter.rs:1457` (`host_cpu_attrs`, the SIGILL path), `llvm_emitter.rs:1476` (a comment banner), `main.rs:733` (`--portable`, untouched). And `avx512_throughput_cycles` - the only thing `has_avx512` gates inside the probe - **is read by nothing**: measured, serialized, parsed back, printed, consulted by no cost model. Re-derive a blast radius rather than inheriting one, as with the phantom `kc-panel loop`.
  - **THE PROBE ITSELF WAS THE ONE PLACE THAT EXECUTES AN AVX-512 INSTRUCTION, GUARDED BY THE READING THAT DOES NOT ANSWER THE QUESTION.** `measure_avx512_throughput` runs a `vpaddd zmm` chain under the raw CPUID bit, so on a machine where CPUID says yes and XCR0 says no the hardware prober **faults** rather than reporting - a SIGILL inside the compiler, on exactly the machines it exists to characterise.
  - **`has_avx` HAD THE IDENTICAL DEFECT AND ONE EXTRA**: it is leaf 1 ECX[28], the **AVX** bit, and `host_cpu_attrs` turns it into `target-cpu=haswell` with **`+avx2`**. A Sandy Bridge has AVX and not AVX2. Fixing one and not the other would be `feedback-guards-consulted-at-one-site`; the new predicate requires `avx2 && avx`, which is what the emitter claims.
  - **`--emit-cpu` WAS CHECKED BEFORE ITS SITE WAS RANKED, and it is a PERFORMANCE fallback, not a correctness one.** `_mm512` and `_mm256` both appear **zero** times in `cpu_emitter.rs`; every regime `CpuShapeDispatcher` can select emits scalar Rust, so a wrong-high answer picks a worse kernel and never faults. Corrected anyway - that is a property of the emitter, not of the decision, and `CpuHardwareProfile::default()` guessing AVX-512 is exactly how `--emit-cpu` came to emit AVX-512 dispatch on every machine the first time. **Distinguish perf fallbacks from correctness ones before ranking them, and fix both.**
  - **THE FIX IS ONE AUTHORITY, AND THE CACHE MAY NOT RAISE THE ANSWER.** `host_has_avx512` is promoted from unused to THE authority, `host_has_avx` added beside it, all four sites routed through them; the cached path **re-probes** and REPORTS a disagreement rather than correcting it silently (`-> NOTE: .ysu_hw_profile says ... this machine reports ... Using the machine.`), on the same principle as naming the assumed card. The machine wins in **both** directions - an AND against the cached value would let a stale `false` suppress a real capability, a regression nothing can see. `--portable` and `Y_NO_AVX512_VNNI` stay the down-only overrides, untouched, and there is deliberately still no override that can CLAIM hardware.
  - **AGREEMENT IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT - THAT IS THE GENERALISABLE PART, AND IT QUALIFIES A RULE THIS FILE ALREADY STATES.** The written precedent is *assert the producers AGREE rather than re-deriving a table*. Followed alone here it produces a **silent** gate: on this machine all four agree, so `the_producers_agree` passes with the bug fully restored - confirmed by mutation (A1/A3), not supposed. What separates the producers is not their output but **which INPUT each consumes**, and where the inputs coincide that is only checkable at the SOURCE. So `the_authority_checks_the_register_state` requires `is_x86_feature_detected!`, forbids `__cpuid` in the authority, and forbids both raw bit-tests reappearing anywhere in the file - the same device as pinning the absence of an env override. **When you write an agreement gate, ask what it would report if every producer were wrong in the same direction.**
  - **MUTATION TABLE, 10 probes, each `--test` target run separately over nine suites.** A1 fresh probe back to raw CPUID / A2 cached path back to the file deciding / A3 `probe_cpu_hardware_profile` back to raw CPUID / A8 the gate stops doctoring the profile / **A5+A9 compound**: **`avx512_probes_agree` ONLY**, all five. A5 over-refusal: `avx512_probes_agree`, two independent assertions. A4 the authority stops checking XCR0: `avx512_probes_agree` + `build_is_warning_free`, **and that second one is my own mutation's unnecessary `unsafe` block, not coverage - a mutation's side effects are not the mutation**. A7 CONTROL, a no-op statement reorder: **green everywhere**, read first, so the table reports the mutations and not the state of the tree.

Hardcoding it is a **no-op here**, so the behavioural assertion pairing width against flag asserts nothing on this machine. Closed by pinning the coupling at the source too. **An assertion pairing two derived values is vacuous wherever they coincide.**

Composed with A5 it IS `feedback-conditional-gates-skip-silently`: measured, `the_fast_path_is_still_taken_on_hardware_that_has_it` reports **ok**, having become a tautology. **THE EXACT GEMM LICENSED HARDWARE IT NEVER ASKED ABOUT, AND THE BICONDITIONAL'S SKIP GUARD WAS THE FUNCTION UNDER TEST (`src/sentinel.rs`, `src/cpu_gemm.rs`, `tests/exact_gemm_requires_its_hardware.rs`).** The item recorded one entry down. `plan_exact_gemm` consulted no hardware at all - it licensed the exact `vpdpwssd` GEMM on operand magnitudes alone - so Y emitted `vpdpwssd` on a machine that has none. This refuses only the FAST path: the scalar lowering still honours `@ZeroDrift` and is still bit-for-bit exact. So getting it wrong conservatively costs time and permissively costs a SIGILL. `the_refusal_does_not_change_the_answer` makes that a measurement rather than a claim - both arms compiled and RUN, compared on a 64-bit checksum **and** a position-weighted sum (a plain sum can agree by cancellation). 512x512x2048: substituted **7.5 ms**, scalar **510 ms**, identical results. The artifact check is `vpdpwssd` **26 -> 0**, and the `#1` attribute group vanishes with the module it belongs to.

The std macro does the `XGETBV` check. **RECORDED, NOT FIXED: `probe_cpu_features` reads leaf 7 EBX bit 16 directly and has that gap**, so `HardwareProfile::has_avx512` can answer `true` where AVX-512 faults; correcting it moves a value cached in `.ysu_hw_profile` that also feeds the analytic cost model, so it wants its own measurement.

Pinned at the SOURCE - the override-guarded return must be `false` - since the absence of a variable cannot be tested by running the compiler.

Its first version skipped when `sentinel::host_has_avx512_vnni()` was false - **so T2, an over-refusal making exactly that function answer `false`, made the test SKIP ITSELF and report ok** while four other suites went red. `feedback-conditional-gates-skip-silently`, inside the test written to prevent it. The guard reads `/proc/cpuinfo` now - a different mechanism entirely - and a non-skippable `the_predicate_agrees_with_the_machine` compares the two readings; two independent sources can only agree by both being right.

T2 over-refusal: the new gate plus four others, after the fix above. T7 the substituted kernel off by one: the new gate plus four others, which is what settles that its 0.20s really compiles and runs two binaries. T6 CONTROL, hardware checked AFTER the licence: green everywhere, so the gate checks the outcome and not the ordering - and the ordering is a message-quality property (a hardware failure is not actionable from the source, so reporting it before a bounds problem stops sending people to fix the wrong thing). T4 was mis-aimed: a `use` inserted before the module doc comment is a build failure, not a result.

Serially: **819 passed, 0 failed, 135 lines**. They contend on `target/`, on shared temp dirs and on `.ysu_hw_profile`. **The tell is the LINE COUNT, not the failures** - an aggregate that stops early reports far fewer result lines than there are targets. **THE DUPLICATE ATTRIBUTE GROUP WAS AN ILLEGAL INSTRUCTION, NOT A SLOW KERNEL - AND MY FIRST TWO MEASUREMENTS OF IT WERE OF DEAD CODE (`src/cpu_gemm.rs`, `tests/emitted_attribute_groups.rs`).** The entry below recorded this and deferred it as "a silent performance regression in the f32 path plus a collision waiting for the next feature". **Both halves of that severity are wrong.** `llvm_emitter::emit_prelude` writes `attributes #0` from the probed host; `emit_vnni_micro_module` is a complete standalone module and wrote `attributes #0` too. A fixture declaring BOTH kernels shows four f32 functions changing. `feedback-null-metrics-pass-dead-components`, in the measurement written to check the claim. **`grep` the ASSEMBLY for the symbol, not the IR.**

After: zero outside the two VNNI functions, which legitimately need it. Same class as the recorded `cpu_emitter` AVX-512 default ("AVX2 runs everywhere AVX-512 does; the reverse crashes"), found again in the LLVM backend, from a group collision instead of a bad default.
  - **PERFORMANCE IS A GENUINE WASH, MEASURED TWICE AT TWO SHAPES.** 512x512x2048, interleaved, best of 40 reps x 8 rounds: f32 **0.727 ms before, 0.729 after**; the exact kernel 6.99 both, its codegen unchanged by construction. `target-cpu="znver5"` buys `f32_matmul` **+395 lines of assembly** and nothing measurable. Checksums identical in every run, float sum included.

The second group was load-bearing all along; the defect is only that it reused `#0`. `VNNI_ATTR_GROUP = "#1"` now, with `IrBuilder::finish_in` naming the group and `finish` keeping `#0`. **A duplicate that is silently discarded and a duplicate that is silently WINNING look identical in the source and have opposite repairs - establish what breaks without the thing before removing it.**

A gate written against one site and validated only at that site has not been shown to generalise, however general its wording.

S6 CONTROL, `#7` instead of `#1`: green everywhere, so the gate checks distinctness rather than a number. S4 probes the gate itself - stop stripping the `# @name` comment from an assembly label and its **non-vacuity floor fires** rather than reporting "no offenders" while parsing nothing.

It reproduced no defect. Re-aimed at ` #1`, the shape the bug had at the new number, it is caught. This is the companion to *check where the mutation landed*: there the edit missed the code, here it hit the code and the code had moved underneath it. **Before recording a survivor, say out loud what defect the mutated program now has.**
