  - **MUTATION TABLE.** Flush clamp operands swapped - **same value, different instructions**: schedule gate FAIL, **all five correctness suites ok**. Second time this session a same-value divergence is caught by this gate and nothing else, and it is the only coverage it uniquely has. Band's extra k moved to the last bands: gate FAIL, `thread_invariance` FAIL. Micro-kernel bypasses the helper writing IDENTICAL text: ok - the design confirmation that the gate checks the property, not the plumbing.
  - **I MISLABELLED A MUTATION IN MY OWN SWEEP AND THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED IT.** I called the band flip "same total"; it is not. `sum_t (base + [t >= rem]) = nthr*base + (nthr - rem)`, which equals `K` only when `rem = nthr - rem` - so it breaks `bands_tile` and the answer moves. **Do the arithmetic on a mutation's label before writing it down**; "same value" is a claim, not a description.
  - **Where extraction stands**: the schedule's ARITHMETIC is extracted (tile width, panel index, flush chunking, K-split bands). The loop nest's SHAPE - which loops exist, in what order, in which blocks, calling what - is still hand-written. That is Phase 2 and is a bigger change than an expression layer.

**THE FIRST SLICE OF THE LOOP NEST IS EXTRACTED RATHER THAN MODELLED, AND THE GATE HAD TO BECOME UNIVERSAL BEFORE IT CAUGHT ANYTHING THE ANSWER COULD NOT (`cpu_gemm::Ix`, `tests/exact_gemm_schedule_proof.rs`).** Phase 1's self-named gap is that the loop STRUCTURE is modelled, so the tie is two models meeting. Closed for one slice by the same move that closed constant drift - **one description, two consumers**, NOT by proving a translator correct (that needs an LLVM semantics and would eat the programme) but by removing the second description. `Ix::emit` renders to the driver's LLVM, `Ix::coq` renders to `proofs/ExactGemmSchedule.v`. Two expressions: `tile_width_ix() = min(ext - iv, T)` at three sites, `panel_index_ix() = iv / T` at two - deliberately the arithmetic §1 of the roadmap says the bugs live in ("twelve address computations correct only because `lda == K` made stride and extent the same number").
  - **THE REFACTOR IS PROVED FAITHFUL BY BYTE-IDENTITY**: all three emitted modules are byte-for-byte what they were. The driver used to spell the clamp as three separate `IrBuilder` calls; it renders it from the shared expression now and emits the same instructions. **Capture the baseline BEFORE touching the emitter** - that identity is the whole evidence the change is behaviour-preserving.
  - Two new theorems are the join that was implicit: `tw` is stated over the tile INDEX and the emitted loop has the induction variable. `the_emitted_width_is_the_tiling_model_at_the_loop_variable` (`tw ext T t = tile_width ext (toff T t) T`) and `the_emitted_panel_index_is_the_tile_index` (`panel_index (toff T t) T = t`, i.e. the emitted `sdiv iv, T` recovers the tile index so a tile reads its OWN panel).
  - **AN EXISTENTIAL GATE IS SATISFIED WHILE ONE SITE OF THREE DIVERGES, AND ONLY A SAME-VALUE MUTATION SHOWS IT.** The first version searched for the rendered instruction sequence ANYWHERE in the module. Swapping the `min` operands at the i-loop computes the **same value** by different instructions - it passed my gate AND all five correctness suites. Counting occurrences PER SITE turns the existential into a universal, and that mutation is now caught **by this gate alone**. That is the gate's only unique coverage, and it is the coverage that matters: a divergence between the proof's arithmetic and the emitter's that no answer can see.
  - **THE OTHER MUTATIONS DO NOT EXTEND COVERAGE AND THE TABLE SAYS SO.** Reversed clamp: gate FAIL, and 3 correctness suites FAIL. Dropped clamp: gate FAIL (after counting), `thread_invariance` FAIL. For those the gate buys a diagnosis by NAME instead of a bad number, not detection. **Run the obvious mutations against the OTHER suites before claiming isolation** - I claimed it once already this session and was wrong.
  - **A hand-written clamp that is IDENTICAL passes, and should.** The gate checks the PROPERTY (the proof's arithmetic is the emitter's arithmetic), not the plumbing (that a helper was called). There is no divergence to catch. That control is what stops the gate degenerating into "did you call my function".
  - **NORMALISING EVERY REGISTER DESTROYS THE DISTINCTION THE TEST EXISTS TO MAKE.** `sub i64 %M, %iv` and `sub i64 %iv, %M` become the same string, and alpha-renaming does not help - both operands are distinct registers under any renaming. Normalise only the BUILDER'S OWN temporaries (`%g12`, `%iv4`) and leave named values (`%M`, `%N`) anchored; that is what makes operand order observable. The non-vacuity control caught this on the first run, which is what a control is for.
  - **The extent is part of the SITE, not of the expression.** Binding `ext` to `%M` everywhere reported 0 matches for the j-loop, which walks `%N`.
  - **What this does NOT close**: which loops exist, in what order, and what they call is still hand-written, and so are the k-split bands and the flush chunking. This is one slice of the nest, not the nest.

**A MUTATION ROW I HAD JUST PUBLISHED WAS MISATTRIBUTED, AND DIAGNOSING IT FOUND THE SCHEDULE'S ONE UNSTATED CONSTRAINT.** The entry below records `VNNI_MR` 6->8 as "caught by 6 model suites", which reads as "six suites detect the drift". **They do not.** `exact_gemm_thread_invariance` - the suite that runs the real threaded kernel at ragged shapes against an independent integer reference and compares bit-identically across thread counts - **PASSES at MR=8**. The kernel is not wrong; it is slow.
  - **SEVEN HARNESSES CARRIED THEIR OWN COPY OF THE TILE SHAPE.** Each embeds a C driver hardcoding `#define MR 6` / `#define NR 64` while its Rust half reads `VNNI_MR`/`VNNI_NR` from the crate (`exact_gemm_{chain,panel,packing_schedule,register_tile,tile_enumeration}_model`, `cpu_gemm_exact_threaded`, `cpu_gemm_vnni_micro`). So moving the constant did not make those tests report a schedule mismatch - it made each test **disagree with ITSELF**: `exact_gemm_panel_model` compared a 48-element panel against a 64-element expectation, and `exact_gemm_register_tile_model`'s child simply crashed (empty stdout, no `DONE`) on buffers sized for the wrong tile. **The same defect `ExactGemmSchedule.v` exists to remove, one layer down, in the half of the harness that allocates the memory the emitted kernel writes into.** All seven take the constants from Rust now - `std::fs::write(&drv, schedule_defines() + DRIVER)`, PREPENDING rather than templating, because C source is full of braces and `format!` is the wrong tool for it. With that fixed, **six of the eight PASS at MR=8**, confirming the original signal was self-disagreement.
  - **WHAT STILL FAILS IS THE REAL CONSTRAINT, AND IT EXISTED ONLY AS A COMMENT.** `cpu_gemm_vnni_micro::the_hot_loop_does_not_spill_the_accumulators`: "hot-loop stack traffic regressed to 17 spills + 17 reloads; it was 10 + 10". That test's own prose already said "24 accumulators + 4 B vectors + 1 A broadcast is 29 of 32 zmm, so the allocator has almost no slack" - and **nothing stated it as a property of the schedule**, not `cpu_gemm.rs` and not any of the nine proofs.
  - **THE PREDICATE IS MEASURED, NOT GUESSED.** Sweeping `VNNI_MR` and reading real compiled spill traffic: MR=5 budget 25/32 within bound; **MR=6 29/32 within bound (10+10, the shipped kernel)**; MR=7 33/32 -> 16+16; MR=8 37/32 -> 17+17. The cliff falls exactly where `MR*NRV + NRV + 1 <= 32` flips, so the FORM of the bound is the measurement's rather than an invention. Now `ExactGemmSchedule.the_tile_fits_the_register_file`, and **it BITES**: with `VNNI_MR = 8` the regenerated file fails `coqc` at that theorem's `lia`, so the generator cannot emit a schedule that does not fit the register file. Nine theorems about an unallocatable tile is not a state this should be able to reach.
  - `ZMM_REGISTERS = 32` is emitted as an **ISA FACT, not a schedule constant** - there is no `cpu_gemm.rs` constant for it and no proof over `nat` establishes it. Same TCB boundary as `vpdpwssd`'s semantics, pinned empirically by the spill test reading real compiled output.
  - **A spilling kernel is SLOW, NOT WRONG, and separating those is what the `thread_invariance` result is for.** That is why the new theorem is a REALIZABILITY constraint rather than a correctness one, and the file says so.
  - **ONE REMAINING MR=8 FAILURE WAS LEFT ALONE, DELIBERATELY.** `exact_gemm_tiling_model::the_unclamped_tail_would_write_past_the_end` asserts `last_off == 48` against a computed `8 * VNNI_MR`. That looks like an eighth hardcode and is not: it mirrors `ExactGemmTiling.unclamped_tail_writes_out_of_bounds`'s CONCRETE counterexample, stated at MR=6. Parameterising it makes the assertion `8*VNNI_MR == 8*VNNI_MR` and worth nothing. Failing when the schedule moves is correct - it says the proof's concrete refutation no longer matches the shipped tile. **Distinguish a hardcode that duplicates a constant from one that pins a fixture to a proof's stated instance.**
  - **The transferable rule: a mutation table row says which tests WENT RED, not which tests DETECTED THE THING.** Reading one row was worth a constraint nobody had written down. Ask what each failure's actual message was before recording the row.

**THE EXACT-GEMM SCHEDULE NOW HAS ONE SOURCE, AND RE-RUNNING A MEASUREMENT THIS FILE'S OWN PROOF HAD RECORDED FOUND IT WRONG (`proofs/ExactGemmSchedule.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_schedule_proof.rs`).** The schedule lived in three places: `cpu_gemm.rs`, the nine proof files (each declaring its own `MR`/`NR`/`col_of`/B-slot-map), and `ExactGemmComposition.v` asserting the copies agree - a theorem somebody remembered to write. `ExactGemmSchedule.v` is GENERATED from `cpu_gemm.rs`'s own constants, committed, and gated on byte-identity; every sibling takes its constants and index maps from it. All nine proofs still compile, no axioms, nothing admitted.
  - **THE MEASUREMENT CAME FIRST AND CORRECTED A WRITTEN CLAIM.** `ExactGemmComposition.v`'s header says each duplicated definition "turns out to be pinned by a theorem in its own file", from three attempts. Those three reproduce, and two more (`RegisterTile.NRV` 4->2, `Packing.NR` 64->32) behave the same - **and `MR` set to 8, in EITHER `ExactGemmPacking` or `ExactGemmRegisterTile`, leaves that file compiling perfectly.** It was never tried. So the pinning was incidental for five definitions of six and ABSENT for the sixth. The honest claim for this work is "makes the pinning structural instead of incidental, and closes one constant that had none" - **nothing had actually drifted**. Header corrected in place, both readings kept.
  - **THE GENERATOR MUST LINK, NOT PARSE - that is the whole design decision.** A `tools/` script would recover `VNNI_MR` with a regex over `cpu_gemm.rs`, i.e. a FOURTH copy of the value living in the generator, which is the bug rather than the fix. `extract_poseidon.py` parses because its input is FOREIGN (circomlib's `.circom`); this input is our own Rust and can be `use`d. That leaves `[[bin]]` or `#[test]`; a fifth `[[bin]]` is a permanent user surface (`tests/source_surface.rs` gates those, the README documents them) bought for a file regenerated twice a year. So: a `#[test]` with `Y_REWRITE_SCHEDULE_PROOF=1`. There is no `build.rs`.
  - **THE CONTENT-CONTROL COLLISION IS A DESIGN DECISION, NOT AN OBSTACLE, AND THE GATE WAS NOT WEAKENED.** `every_proof_has_a_content_control` rejects a `.v` naming no load-bearing theorem, so a definitions-only generated file fails it. It takes **no exemption**. Two of its theorems are STRUCTURAL - they constrain the shape of the emitted expressions rather than restating values, so being generated alongside what they describe does not make them true: `slot_b_is_the_plain_interleave` (the two sides come from different places in `cpu_gemm.rs` - `pack_b_slot`, and the bare `/2` `panel_slot_decode` inverts it with) and `the_tile_geometry_is_consistent` (`NR = NRV*LANES`, no degenerate zero; **`LANES` is DERIVED in the generator as `VNNI_NR / VNNI_NRV` rather than written down, so it cannot become a fourth copy of 16**). A third, `ksplit_threads_is_never_zero`, is a genuine cross-file join: every theorem in `ExactGemmKsplit.v` is stated under `0 < nthr` and nothing proved the emitted thread count satisfies it - the floor was argued in a comment. The fourth, `the_schedule_is_the_shipped_one`, IS self-fulfilling under generation and the file says so; its job is the other direction, making a hand-edit fail `coqc` as well as byte-identity.
  - **`slot_b` and `slot_b_interleave` are deliberately NOT collapsed.** Collapsing the emitted `vpdpwssd` vector-group form into the plain interleave would make `slot_b_is_the_plain_interleave` and `ExactGemmComposition.the_agreement_is_not_vacuous` true by `reflexivity` and worth nothing - which that file's own control already says.
  - **TWO THEOREM STATEMENTS CHANGED TEXT, DECLARED RATHER THAN SLIPPED THROUGH.** `ExactGemmMicro.the_default_interval_licenses_4095_and_not_4096` and `the_4096_case_exceeds_by_exactly_one` carried the flush interval as a bare `64` - the ONLY place in the nine proofs where a schedule constant sat inside a STATEMENT. They read `SCH.FLUSH_K_PAIRS` now: same proposition at the shipped value, but a drift in `DEFAULT_FLUSH_K_PAIRS` now makes them FALSE and fails `coqc` rather than quietly pinning an interval the compiler no longer uses. 4095/4096 stay literals on purpose - they are the LICENCE's answer at that interval (`floor(sqrt(i32::MAX / 2Fl))`), not a schedule constant, and stating them is what makes the edge one unit wide. Every other statement is byte-identical; the siblings gained only `*_unfold` helpers proved by `reflexivity`.
  - **MUTATION TABLE, thirteen suites, each `--test` target run SEPARATELY.** Rust `VNNI_MR` 6->8: schedule gate FAIL, 6 model suites FAIL. **Rust `KSPLIT_MIN_BAND` 128->256: schedule gate FAIL and NOTHING ELSE** - the clearest single justification, since no model test in the repo compares that constant against anything. Committed `.v` hand-edited `MR := 8`: schedule gate and `proofs_are_checked` FAIL, **all eleven model suites pass** - they drive the Rust and never read the proofs, so the Coq-side half of the drift was uncovered entirely. `RegisterTile.NR := SCH.MR`: byte-identity correctly does NOT fire (the generated file is untouched) and `Composition.the_tile_shape_is_the_same_everywhere` does - a CONFIRMATION that the agreement theorems' weakened claim ("each file aliases the right thing", rather than "two independent definitions coincide") is still real.
  - **A SURVIVOR THAT WAS A HOLE IN MY OWN CONTROL, and it is `feedback-null-metrics-pass-dead-components` for the second time in a file written to apply it.** Neutering the generator to echo the committed file left the byte-identity gate passing AND the control passing, because the control asserted the output *contains* `Definition MR : nat := 6.` - which the committed file contains. The gate had become a check on a constant string with the whole run green. It renders a **PERTURBED** schedule now and requires the result to differ from the committed text, which an echoing generator cannot do. **When a generator is gated on byte-identity against its own output, the control must exercise the generator at an input that is NOT the committed one.**
  - A second survivor was genuinely mis-aimed: `Schedule::shipped` reading `mr: 6` instead of `mr: VNNI_MR` changes nothing observable, the two being the same number. Hardcode `6` AND move `VNNI_MR` to 8, or read the wrong constant outright (`mr: VNNI_NRV`), and the tie assertion fails in both. **Confirm a mutation changes the program before recording a survivor** - a hardcode that agrees today is caught the moment it stops agreeing.
  - **What this does NOT close**: the loop NEST is still hand-written `IrBuilder` calls in `cpu_gemm.rs`, and the tie between the models and the emitted LLVM is still two models meeting. This closes constant drift, not extraction. Extraction is Phase 2.

**THE PACKING SCHEDULE IS TIED TO THE RUNNING DRIVER TOO, AND FOUR OF SIX MUTATIONS ARE CAUGHT BY NOTHING ELSE (`tests/exact_gemm_packing_schedule.rs`).** The tile enumeration covers the driver's tile loop; its OTHER loop — the one preparing the panels — was guarded only by a paragraph in `emit_vnni_gemm_driver`'s doc comment ("B was re-packed once per ROW panel — `M/MR` times over … At MR=6 that is a sixth of the total run"). **A re-packing bug is invisible in the answer**: packing A inside the j-loop, or B inside the i-loop, computes exactly the right result and merely does `ntn`/`ntm` times the work. Same shape as `a_deep_constant_chain_collapses_completely` (a convergence property needing a SIZE assertion) and the shared-memory swizzle (a performance property needing a measurement).
  - **Same excision technique as the enumeration test, applied to all THREE callees at once.** `__y_gemm_vnni_pack_a`, `__y_gemm_vnni_pack_b` and `__y_gemm_micro_vnni` are excised and replaced by `declare`s with recording C stubs. The two packers are `internal`, so the excision has to match `define internal void @…` as well as `define void @…`; a `declare` is never `internal`.
  - **Recording all three in ONE event stream is what makes the schedule checkable rather than three counts.** The whole of it is one assertion — `[A(0)..A(ntm-1)] ++ concat over j of ([B(j)] ++ [K(0)..K(ntm-1)])` — which says at once that every A pack precedes every B pack, that there are `ntm` and `ntn` of them rather than `ntm*ntn`, and that each B panel is **live for exactly its own column's tiles**, not merely written the right number of times.
  - **I PREDICTED THE UNCLAMPED-PACKER MUTATIONS WOULD BE CAUGHT BY THE CORRECTNESS SUITES, WROTE THAT IN THE DOCSTRING, AND MEASURING SAID OTHERWISE.** Dropping either packer's clamp AT THE CALL SITE makes it read up to `MR-1` rows past the end of `A` or `NR-1` columns past the end of `B` — and every answer stays bit-identical, because the FOLD-BACK's own `mw`/`nw` clamp discards exactly the rows and columns the packer over-read. **The observable consequence of a live out-of-bounds READ is nothing at all**, until the buffer ends at a page boundary. That is the redundant-guard pattern `exact_gemm_packing_model` already records for the masks INSIDE the packers, one layer up at the call site — and it is why "the correctness suites cover the packers" is false.

    | mutation | pack_sched | tile_enum | tiling_model | thr-inv | exact-thr | packing_model |
    |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    | **A packed inside the j-loop** | **caught** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
    | **B packed inside the i-loop** | **caught** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
    | **pack_a's row count unclamped (`MR`)** | **caught** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
    | **pack_b's column count unclamped (`NR`)** | **caught** | ok | ok | ok | ok | ok |
    | A panel offset is the row index, not the tile index | caught | ok | caught | caught | caught | caught |
    | both packers handed `K-1` | caught | ok | caught | caught | caught | caught |

  - **`exact_gemm_tile_enumeration` catches NONE of the six**, which is the result saying the two files are complementary rather than overlapping — it excises the micro-kernel only, so what the packers are handed and in what order is invisible to it. Between them they cover the driver's two loops: that one the tiles it visits, this one the panels it prepares.
  - **THE SHARED-TEMP-DIR RACE, FIFTH OCCURRENCE, IN A FILE I WROTE TWO COMMITS AGO.** `exact_gemm_panel_model.rs`'s `build()` was pid-only and called from two tests; it had been green for two commits and fired the moment a new test binary changed the scheduling — the "passed for several runs before failing" signature exactly. `tests/` was then SWEPT for the same defect rather than waiting for a sixth: the two other candidates are false positives (`ptx_intrinsics_assemble.rs` shares a directory but names files per-`name` and never deletes it; `ptx_shared_memory.rs`'s hit was a `main(` inside an embedded Y source string). The suite is clean now. **The detector is worth keeping in mind: a `temp_dir().join(format!(..))` whose only interpolated value is `process::id()`, in a helper with two or more call sites, in a file that calls `remove_dir_all`.**
  - **The fish word-splitting trap, THIRD occurrence, in the mutation harness itself.** `SUITES="a b c"; for S in $SUITES` passes the whole string as ONE argument in fish, so the first sweep reported one column per mutation instead of six and every row read `CAUGHT`. The tell was that the "suite name" printed was the entire list. Run a multi-target sweep from a `bash` script file, not from an interactive fish command.

**THE TILE ENUMERATION IS NOW TIED TO THE RUNNING DRIVER (`tests/exact_gemm_tile_enumeration.rs`).** The capstone assumes the driver visits tile `(r/MR, c/NR)` for every position; nothing had asked the emitted driver how many tiles it runs or in what order. **A correct tiling is invisible in the answer** (`c_written_exactly_once` is that statement), so the answer cannot arbitrate it — the same bind the K-split was in, where the spawn count was the only observable. Here the observable is the sequence of micro-kernel invocations.
  - **`--wrap` DOES NOT WORK for an intra-module call.** `__y_gemm_micro_vnni` is called from the driver in the same module, so the call is resolved at compile time and there is no relocation for the linker to redirect (unlike `pthread_create`, which is external). The module instead has that definition **excised** and replaced by a `declare`, with the C driver supplying a recording stub; the driver under test is byte-identical otherwise. That trick generalises to any intra-module callee.
  - Three things pinned: the call count is `mn_tiles(M,MR).len() * mn_tiles(N,NR).len()`; the ORDER is column-panel outer, row-panel inner (which is what makes "B is packed once per column panel" a checked fact rather than a comment); and every call gets the FULL `kpairs` and `ldc = NR`.
  - **WHAT IT ISOLATES IS LESS THAN IT FIRST LOOKED, AND THE TABLE SAYS SO.** Five driver mutations: row loop strides by `MR-1`, column loop by `2*NR`, half the k-pairs, scratch stride `ldc` — **all four caught by every suite**, because they change the answer. The fifth, **one extra row panel past M**, is clamped to zero width so the fold-back writes nothing and **the answer is unchanged**: caught by `tile_enum` and `thr-inv`, MISSED by `tiling_model`, `exact-thr`, `packing` and `chain`. So the honest claim is "covers enumeration errors that do not change the answer, and diagnoses the rest by name instead of as a bad number" — not "catches what the others cannot". **Run the obvious mutations before claiming isolation; four of five said nothing.**
  - **The shared-temp-dir race, FOURTH occurrence.** It is a property of the `build()` helper, not of any one test, so the per-test tag now lives in the signature rather than in a comment asking the next author to remember.

**ALL SIX EXACT-GEMM PROOFS ARE NOW CHAINED, AND THE ENTRY BEFORE THIS ONE NAMED THE WRONG GAP (`proofs/ExactGemmWhole.v`).** `the_threaded_gemm_holds_the_source_dot_products`: sum the partials of `nthr` threads, each handed a K band, each running the emitted driver — packing, routing, the k-pair loop, the int32 flush, the scratch tile and the fold-back — and for every `(r, c)` inside `M x N` the result is exactly `sum_k A[r][k] * B[k][c]`. **No hypothesis that `MR` divides `M`, `NR` divides `N`, `nthr` divides `K`, or that `K` is even.** 6 `Print Assumptions`, no axioms. The only assumption is the licence, discharged by exhausting int16 in `exact_gemm_licence_obligations.rs`.
  - **THE PREVIOUS ENTRY'S "what is missing" WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, and reading the emitter is what settled it.** It named a **kc-panel loop** (K cut into panels of `kc` inside one thread) as the layer proved nowhere, and guessed it was "probably cheap" because it resembles `bands_tile`. **There is no such loop**: `emit_vnni_gemm_driver` passes the FULL `K` to both packers and `kpairs = (K+1)/2` to the micro-kernel, and the only cut of the K axis is the K-split across threads. So `kc` in every sibling file IS K, and the gap that actually remained was the **fold-back into C**. **Read the emitter before recording a gap** — a guess from structural resemblance named a layer that does not exist while missing the one that did.
  - The two joins: `the_position_is_live_in_its_own_tile` (`r` lands in tile `r/T` at offset `r mod T`, and the clamped width covers it — so the store predicate is TRUE for every live position) and `the_position_decomposition_is_the_tilings` (the `(r, c)` view addresses the same element as `ExactGemmTiling`'s `(tile, offset)` view, so `c_written_exactly_once` applies).
  - **NO NEW BEHAVIOURAL TEST, DELIBERATELY.** `exact_gemm_thread_invariance.rs` already runs M=53, N=71, K=4099 — all three ragged against the 6x64 tile — at 1/2/3/5/8/16 threads against an independent integer reference; `cpu_gemm_exact_threaded.rs` sweeps flush intervals across the same; `exact_gemm_tiling_model.rs` covers a padded `ldc`. That IS this theorem's tie. **A fourth near-duplicate would add coverage of nothing** — check what the existing suite already exercises before writing the obvious companion test.
  - **What remains is now exactly ONE structural gap, and it is Phase 2's.** `vpdpwssd`'s semantics and the i32 half-order are DEFINITIONS pinned by `cpu_gemm_vnni_micro.rs` on hardware; and the loop STRUCTURE is modelled rather than extracted — `gemm_position` says what `(r, c)` receives on the reading that the driver visits tile `(r/MR, c/NR)` at offset `(r mod MR, c mod NR)`. The tie is between two models, not to the emitted LLVM.
  - Mutation-verified 4/4 (column offset at `mod MR`, drop `r < M`, read band `t` not `t'`, scale the row by `NR` in the address tie).

**THE TILE LIFT, AND THE TEST GAP IT EXPOSED IS WORTH MORE THAN THE THEOREM (`proofs/ExactGemmChain.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_chain_model.rs`).** `the_tile_holds_the_source_dot_products` takes the lane statement to the whole `MR x NR` tile: for every live `(i, j)`, `C[i][j] = C0[i][j] + sum_k A[i][k]*B[k][j]`, and for every dead one `C[i][j] = C0[i][j]` exactly. 18 `Print Assumptions`, no axioms.
  - **The join needed is the INVERSE of `col_of`.** `RT.tile_position_surjective` says an inverse exists; `the_lane_map_is_a_two_sided_inverse` names it (`vec_of j = j/16`, `lane_of j = j mod 16`) and proves it inverts BOTH ways — which is what licenses `distinct_columns_use_distinct_lanes`, i.e. no two tile positions share an accumulator lane, so 384 values live in 24 registers of 16 lanes with nothing aliasing.
  - **THE STORE PREDICATE DOES NO WORK, AND THAT IS A THEOREM.** The emitted micro-kernel writes all `MR*NR` positions unconditionally — the live-rectangle clamp is the DRIVER's — so the tile model was carrying two things at once. `the_store_predicate_is_redundant` shows a dead row or column accumulates zero by the packers' masks, so adding it to `C0` leaves `C0`. It settles the faithfulness question (the tile theorem describes the micro-kernel's OWN effect on C, clamp or no clamp) and it is **the proved twin of a redundancy `exact_gemm_packing_model.rs` had only MEASURED**. Note the asymmetry: `a_dead_position_leaves_c_untouched` holds unconditionally BECAUSE of the predicate; the redundancy needs the licence hypotheses, which is why dropping the predicate from the definition fails the file.
  - **THE BEHAVIOURAL GAP THE THEOREM EXPOSED IS THE MORE USEFUL HALF: the tile theorem says `C0 + dot` and the driver ZEROED C, so the accumulate clause was never exercised.** A kernel that ASSIGNS rather than accumulates is indistinguishable from a correct one when C starts at zero and there is one flush chunk. The test now runs every shape twice, C zeroed and C pre-loaded. **Demonstrated load-bearing rather than assumed**: with the multi-chunk shapes removed so `kc = 133` cannot do the work, mutating the flush to overwrite C is caught ONLY on the pre-loaded arm, at the first shape (384/384 positions). Pre-loading is also the only way "a dead position is left as it was" is testable at all — with C zeroed, *untouched* and *zeroed* are the same observation. **When a theorem gains a term (`C0 +`), check the test supplies a non-trivial value for it.**
  - **Still missing to reach the whole of C, NAMED rather than left to be discovered**: `ExactGemmTiling.v`'s output partition and `ExactGemmKsplit.v`'s bands are each proved over their own model and not joined to this one; and the **kc-panel loop** (cutting K into panels of `kc` inside one thread) is proved NOWHERE. It is the same decomposition shape as `ExactGemmKsplit.bands_tile`, so probably cheap — "probably cheap" is not "done".
  - Mutation-verified 4/4 on the proof (`vec_of` at /32, `lane_of` at mod 8, drop the `j < NR` bound, drop the store predicate).
  - **`proofs/` now gitignores Rocq artifacts.** The gate compiles in a temp dir precisely so they never appear, but every proof header tells a reader to run `coqc` by hand, which drops `.lia.cache` beside the source — as mine did, and it showed up in `git status` as an untracked file. A gate that avoids an artifact does not stop the DOCUMENTED command from producing it.

**THE CHAIN CLOSES FOR ONE ACCUMULATOR LANE, AND THE TWO INDEPENDENT MODELS TURNED OUT TO MEET (`proofs/ExactGemmChain.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_chain_model.rs`).** `the_emitted_lane_computes_the_source_dot_product`: the emitted flush schedule, accumulating each chunk in **int32** and adding into an int64 running sum, over the panels the emitted packers produce, through the emitted routing, gives lane `l` of vector `v` for row `i` exactly `sum_k A[i][k] * B[k][16v+l]` — the **source** matrices' dot product. No hypothesis on panel contents, none that the flush interval divides the k-pair count, none that the tile is full. 11 `Print Assumptions`, no axioms.
  - **The connective tissue is the content, and it was not obviously going to fit.** `kloop_is_the_padded_product` turns a loop of routing steps into the padded product `ExactGemmPacking` already evaluates; `kloop_is_sum_from_step` re-presents the same loop in the shape `ExactGemmMicro`'s flush theorem quantifies over. Those two models were written in different sessions for different obligations — `sum_pairs` counts k-PAIRS carrying both halves, `sum_from` is a flat range — so each join is a real lemma, not a definitional coincidence. **That they met at all is the first evidence the five-file split was the right decomposition rather than five unrelated models.**
  - **The licence is load-bearing for the WHOLE chain, refuted symbolically and behaviourally at the same numbers.** `violating_the_licence_breaks_the_chain` evaluates the chain at magnitude 4096 with the shipped interval 64 and gets **-2,147,483,648 where the answer is 2,147,483,648**; the control at 4095 is exact. The Rust tie reaches the identical pair on the real `vpdpwssd` kernel **from source matrices through the real packers**, where `exact_gemm_micro_model.rs` reaches it only with hand-built panels. Same one-unit boundary as `the_4096_case_exceeds_by_exactly_one`, now at end-to-end scope.
  - **`kc = 133` is deliberate: 67 k-pairs against a 64-pair interval, so the clamped final chunk is a real case.** No sibling model test crosses a flush boundary. Mutating the flush to OVERWRITE `C` rather than accumulate — invisible with one chunk, since C is zeroed — is caught.
  - **WHAT IT DOES NOT CATCH IS RECORDED BESIDE WHAT IT DOES, and the last row is the point.** Five emitter mutations across every exact-GEMM suite: flush-overwrites `packing/thr-inv/exact-thr/chain` FAIL; `pack_b` stride 32->16 `packing/panel/thr-inv/exact-thr/chain` FAIL; `pack_b` mask dropped **panel and chain only**; **compensating pair (`pack_b v^1` AND store column `v^1`) — panel and regtile FAIL, chain OK.** The chain test composes packing with routing, so an inverse pair cancels there exactly as in a full GEMM. **Adding a test does not retire the tests it resembles**, and the register-tile file's own table is now dated by this (it predates `exact_gemm_panel_model.rs`, which catches the pair by the other route — checking the panel slot by slot instead of stating it).
  - **Still not chained, stated in the file**: one LANE not the tile (the tile needs the store, over a different model of C); it does not reach `C` through `ExactGemmTiling`'s partition or `ExactGemmKsplit`'s bands, both of which sit ABOVE it over their own models; `vpdpwssd`'s semantics and the i32 half-order remain definitions pinned by `tests/cpu_gemm_vnni_micro.rs`. Joining the rest needs one shared kernel model — Phase 2.
  - **THE TEMP-DIR RACE, HIT FOR THE THIRD TIME IN THIS REPO.** Both tests in the new file called one `build()` using `format!("y_chain_{}", process::id())`, so one test's `remove_dir_all` landed while the other was writing its IR — presenting as `write IR` failing with the module perfectly valid. Previously seen in the GPU `.ptx` harness and in `tests/backend_differential.rs`. **A per-test tag is not decoration; any helper that materialises files in a temp dir needs one.**
  - Mutation-verified 8/8: four against the emitter (above), four against the proof (drop the licence bound, drop `0 < Fl`, seed the accumulator at 1, read the next k-pair group's base). **One mutation I tried first was a semantic NO-OP** — `icmp slt` -> `sle` on `cend0` vs `kpairs`, which gives the same `select` at equality. A green sweep from a no-op mutation is not a test hole; check the mutation actually changes the program before recording a survivor.

**THE ONE ASSUMED STEP OF PHASE 1 IS DISCHARGED, AND TRYING TO VIOLATE IT FIRST IS WHAT FOUND IT WAS WRONG (`proofs/ExactGemmPacking.v`, `ExactGemmComposition.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_panel_model.rs`).** The composition file named its own seam - two hypotheses about what the packed panels hold, written down rather than buried - and the next thing done to it was to ask whether a REAL panel satisfies them. **It does not.** They quantified over every `i` and `j`, and at `i = MR` the index named, `p*(2*MR) + 2*MR`, is the FIRST slot of k-pair group `p+1`, which holds that group's data; an unbounded contract demands a zero there whenever row `MR` is past `mrows`. So the composition was true and **unusable** - applying it meant supplying a premise satisfied only by a panel one k-pair group long. Not vacuous (it is satisfiable), which is why nothing complained: **a satisfiable hypothesis that the object of study does not satisfy is a proof about something else.**
  - **A hypothesis nothing is shown to satisfy is the proof-shaped version of a licence nothing can violate.** This repo already runs that check on its licences - `the_add_formula_really_is_incomplete`, `garbage_in_the_pad_changes_the_answer`, `the_4096_case_exceeds_by_exactly_one` - and had never run it on its own premises. **When a file says "this step is assumed", the next move is to try to satisfy the assumption, not to leave the note.**
  - The discharge is `ExactGemmPacking.panel` - the panel modelled as a FUNCTION, decoding an index into `(group, row-or-column, half)` - plus `panel_decodes_its_own_write` (the contract, with `idx < width`) and **`panel_is_the_only_solution`**, which proves ANY array satisfying the packer's writes agrees with `panel` over the whole panel range. That second one is what makes the first a claim about the emitted loop instead of about a model chosen to make the composition go through, and it is where the bijection lemmas finally pay at panel scale: injective => the write spec is consistent, onto => it is complete. `the_packed_panels_route_to_the_right_source_elements` is then the composition with no hypothesis about panel contents at all.
  - **The behavioural tie runs the REAL packers rather than a transcription.** `__y_gemm_vnni_pack_a`/`_pack_b` are `internal`, so the test appends two exported wrappers to the emitted module and calls them from C; panels are POISONED (`-31337`) so an unwritten slot fails instead of reading back as a plausible zero; five shapes (full, phantom k-half, ragged M, ragged N, all three) with **every stride differing from its extent**; every slot compared against `panel_slot_decode`.
  - **IT ISOLATES WHAT NO END-TO-END TEST CAN, AND THAT WAS MEASURED.** The packing entry already records that removing `pack_b`'s zero-fill ALONE leaves every answer correct - a padding term is `a_pad * b_pad`, so a zero on either side kills it, and the two masks could only ever be pinned as a conjunction. With `pack_b`'s mask dropped: `exact_gemm_packing_model` ok, `exact_gemm_thread_invariance` ok, `cpu_gemm_exact_threaded` ok, `exact_gemm_tiling_model` ok, **`exact_gemm_panel_model` FAILED**. Same shape as the register tile's compensating-pair table, one layer down.
  - Mutation-verified 8/8 - four against the emitted packers and the decode (halves swapped, A group stride, B vector stride 32->16, mask dropped), four against the proofs (drop `idx < width`, revert the contract to unbounded, break the decode, drop the range bound on uniqueness). **The unbounded-contract mutation now fails where the previous commit compiled it happily**, which is the evidence that the discharge is what pins the bound.
  - **A GATE BUG FELL OUT OF WRITING THE PROSE, and then probing the fix found an older one.** `nothing_in_any_proof_is_admitted` stripped Coq comments LINE-LOCALLY (`line.split("(*").next()`), so a continuation line inside a multi-line comment was scanned as CODE - a paragraph containing the ordinary English word "admit" failed the build. Contorting the prose would have left the hole; Coq comments also NEST, so a depth counter is not optional. Probing the fixed gate with what it exists to catch then found the older hole: it tested `code == "Admitted."`, `starts_with("admit")` and `contains(" admit.")`, and **`Proof. Admitted.` on ONE line - the commonest way to stub a Coq lemma - is none of the three.** It matches the TOKEN now and also covers `Abort.`, which discards the lemma outright while the file still compiles. **A gate passes every real file perfectly while holed; only feeding it the thing it guards against says otherwise.**

**THE FIVE EXACT-GEMM PROOFS NOW MEET, AND THE FILE THAT JOINS THEM CORRECTED ITS OWN PREMISE (`proofs/ExactGemmComposition.v`).** Each of the five was written self-contained, so three of them define the B panel's slot map - `ExactGemmPacking.slot_b` as the emitted `(j/16)*32 + (j%16)*2 + h`, `ExactGemmMicro.slot` and `ExactGemmRegisterTile.slot_b` as the plain `2j + h` - and `MR`, `NR`, `col_of` are each defined twice. Nothing checked they agreed. `Require` (not `Require Import`) plus qualified names lets the agreement be stated; `the_proof_gate` already resolves an acyclic `Require` graph, so no harness change was needed.
  - **THE HEADER'S FIRST DRAFT OVERSTATED THE RISK, AND MEASURING IT IS WHAT SHOWED THAT.** I wrote "each file would go on type-checking while proving a theorem about a kernel the others no longer describe", then went looking for a drift that is invisible in-file. **Three attempts, all CAUGHT by the file itself**: `RegisterTile.slot_b` shifted by one, its `NR` set to 32, and `Micro.slot` with the two halves swapped (that last by a brittle proof script rather than by a statement - weaker, still a gate). So every definition is already pinned by a theorem in its own file, by accident of what that file happens to prove. The agreement theorems make the pinning EXPLICIT and cross-file rather than incidental, which is a smaller and true claim. **Check a claim about what would go unnoticed by trying to make it go unnoticed.**
  - **The composition step is the real new content, and it is the one thing no single file can state**: `the_lane_accumulates_the_source_elements` says one `vpdpwssd` step on the packed panels contributes exactly the two k-terms of the SOURCE matrices' dot product for `(row i, column 16v+l)`, masked. Packing says what a slot holds; the register tile says which lane reads it; only together do they say the lane reads the right source element. `a_dead_row_contributes_nothing` shows the masking survives the composition rather than needing re-argument at each layer.
  - **The packers' contract is a HYPOTHESIS, not a re-derivation, and naming that is the point.** `ExactGemmPacking.v` proves the slot maps are bijections and that the padded product equals the live dot product; it does not state "slot `s` holds source element `x`" as one reusable lemma. So the composition assumes it explicitly - **that is the one step of Phase 1 that is assumed rather than proved**, and the file says so instead of hiding it in a definition.
  - **What is still NOT composed, stated in the file**: this joins packing to routing for ONE `vpdpwssd` step. It does not chain that through the k-pair loop into the flush, nor through the output partition, nor through the K-split, into a single "the emitted kernel equals the naive nest". Each of those is proved over its own model; a genuine end-to-end theorem needs one shared model of the kernel, which is Phase 2's work rather than a missing lemma.

**THE REGISTER TILE'S ROUTING IS PROVED, AND THE TEST THAT GUARDS IT NEEDED A COMPENSATING-PAIR MUTATION TO JUSTIFY ITSELF (`proofs/ExactGemmRegisterTile.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_register_tile_model.rs`).** `the_lane_consumes_its_own_column` proves the emitted broadcast + the four `<32 x i16>` loads at `Bp + p*NR*2 + v*32` + `vpdpwssd` send panel slot `2j+h` to the accumulator lane whose store column is `j` - the join between `ExactGemmPacking.v` (what a slot holds) and the kernel (which lane reads it). `the_i32_load_is_the_packed_pair` proves the `getelementptr inbounds i32` at element `p*MR+i` aliases packed slots `2i`/`2i+1` of group `p`. Rocq 9.1, 8 `Print Assumptions`, no axioms.
  - **A SINGLE-SITE MUTATION CANNOT JUSTIFY AN ISOLATION TEST - only a compensating pair can.** I wrote the docstring claiming the full-GEMM tests could not catch a routing bug, then checked: breaking the B vector offset alone **fails every GEMM test in the repo**, so the claim as written was FALSE. The real claim is about inverse bugs, and it is now demonstrated: XOR the vector index in BOTH `emit_vnni_pack_b` (`v := v ^ 1`) and the flush's store column (`c = (v ^ 1) * 16`) and they cancel - `exact_gemm_packing_model`, `exact_gemm_thread_invariance` and `cpu_gemm_exact_threaded` all report **ok** while the register-tile test FAILS. Driving `__y_gemm_micro_vnni` directly with hand-built panels removes the composition, so there is nothing left for a packer to compensate with. **Check a claim about what other tests cannot catch by running them under the mutation.**
  - **The masked tails are here too, and they EXPLAIN the packing entry's measurement.** `a_padding_column_never_reaches_c` / `a_padding_row_never_reaches_c` are why the packers' row and column masks are redundant, while the phantom k-half's - which contributes to a LIVE column - is not. The measured table one section down and these two theorems are the same fact from two sides.
  - **`vpdpwssd` and little-endianness are DEFINITIONS, not theorems**, and the file says so; they are pinned by `tests/cpu_gemm_vnni_micro.rs` on the real instruction. `swapping_the_pair_halves_computes_a_different_function` makes the endianness assumption load-bearing, with `a_symmetric_operand_hides_the_swap` as the control - which is why the fixture is asymmetric in every axis. Phase 1 now has the whole schedule plus the tile's routing; what it does not have is a machine-checked model of the instruction itself, which no proof over `Z` can supply.

**PHASE 1'S FOURTH AND LAST SCHEDULE THEOREM IS THE FLUSH, AND IT MADE THE LICENCE'S NECESSITY BEHAVIOURAL (`proofs/ExactGemmMicro.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_micro_model.rs`).** `vpdpwssd` accumulates into int32, which wraps; the kernel runs a bounded number of k-pairs into int32 and then widens into an int64 running sum. `flush_exact` proves the chunks `[c, min(c+F, kpairs))` sum to the whole range with no hypothesis that `F` divides `kpairs`; `flush_exact_in_int32` models int32 with an explicit `wrap32` and proves it agrees with `Z` exactly when no partial sum leaves the range; `operand_bound_gives_no_overflow` derives that hypothesis from `2*F*m^2 <= i32::MAX`, which is exactly what `VnniExact::max_operand_magnitude` computes. Rocq 9.1, 8 `Print Assumptions`, no axioms. **The flush chunking is the CLAMPED-TILE shape of `ExactGemmTiling.v`, NOT the uneven-band shape of `ExactGemmKsplit.v`** - a flush interval is a fixed overflow budget, not a work split, and confusing them points a schedule proof at the wrong theorem.
  - **IS THE LICENCE NECESSARY, OR IS IT PAPERWORK? Nothing had asked.** `cpu_gemm_exact_threaded.rs` links three flush intervals into one process and compares bit for bit, so interval INVARIANCE was covered; the other direction was not. `emit_vnni_micro_module` takes the interval directly, so the emitted symbols can be driven past the bound even though the compiler refuses to. At `K = 128` (`kpairs = 64`, exactly one default interval) with CONSTANT operands - the bound is a worst case random data never reaches - magnitude 4095 gives the exact 2,146,435,200 and magnitude **4096 returns -2,147,483,648 where the answer is 2,147,483,648**. So the one-unit-wide boundary that `exact_gemm_licence_obligations.rs` finds by exhausting int16, and that `the_4096_case_exceeds_by_exactly_one` states as arithmetic, is now observable in a running kernel. **A licence nothing can violate is indistinguishable from a licence that certifies nothing** - the same shape as `garbage_in_the_pad_changes_the_answer` and `the_add_formula_really_is_incomplete`. Mutation M6 is what makes it non-vacuous: forcing the emitter to flush every k-pair, so no overflow is possible, fails the test.
  - **THE FIRST CROSS-FILE OBLIGATION IN THIS SERIES, and it guards a failure nothing else can see.** `ExactGemmPacking.v` says `pack_b` puts column `j`'s `h`-th k-value at slot `2j + h`; `vpdpwssd` consumes that slot in vector `slot/32`, lane `(slot mod 32)/2`; the store writes vector `v` lane `l` to column `16v + l`. `the_packed_column_is_the_stored_column` proves the composition is the identity. A mismatch is a correctly-summed but **column-PERMUTED** tile - every partial sum right, every value in the wrong place, and no bijection or bound in any other file able to notice. The control `a_wrong_lane_stride_permutes_the_columns` stops it being satisfied by any pair of maps that merely compose.
  - **`malloc`/`free` are declared by `llvm_emitter`'s PRELUDE, not by either `cpu_gemm` module**, so neither module is self-contained when emitted standalone and `emit_vnni_threaded_module`'s `need_libc_decls` flag does not cover them. The sibling tests never hit this because they compile a `.ysu` through the real binary and inherit the prelude. Worth knowing before writing another standalone harness.
  - **What is still NOT proved, stated in the file**: the 2-D register tile and the masked tails. A lane's contribution is taken as GIVEN rather than derived from the packed panels, so nothing says the accumulator for row `i` is fed row `i`'s broadcast. That and `vpdpwssd`'s own semantics are ISA facts pinned by `tests/cpu_gemm_vnni_micro.rs`. Phase 1's SCHEDULE is complete - K-split reduction, output partition, packing, flush - and the kernel's arithmetic core is what remains.

**PHASE 1'S THIRD THEOREM IS THE OPERAND PACKING, AND ITS MOST USEFUL RESULT IS NEGATIVE (`proofs/ExactGemmPacking.v`, `tests/exact_gemm_packing_model.rs`).** `pack_a`/`pack_b` move a live `MR x kc` / `kc x NR` tile into a contiguous panel that the micro-kernel then runs at FULL width however ragged the tile was. `pack_a_slot_bijective` / `pack_b_slot_bijective` (with `_in_panel`, `_onto`) say nothing is written twice and no slot keeps the previous tile; `padded_product_is_the_live_dot_product` is THE theorem - the full `kpairs*2` product over the padded panel equals the dot product over the live `kc` - and `garbage_in_the_pad_changes_the_answer` refutes the zero-fill-free version concretely, so the `select ... i16 0` is machine-checked as load-bearing rather than asserted to be. Rocq 9.1, 9 `Print Assumptions`, no axioms, nothing admitted. With this the SCHEDULE is complete (K-split reduction, output partition, packing); what stays unproved is the micro-kernel itself - the 2-D register tile, the masked tails and the int32 accumulate whose no-overflow obligation is discharged exhaustively over the finite int16 domain in `tests/exact_gemm_licence_obligations.rs`.
  - **A DECOMPOSITION THAT FOLDS IS NOT A DIFFERENT FUNCTION, and this repo was claiming it was.** `pack_b`'s destination map is emitted as `(j/16)*32 + (j%16)*2 + h` to document the `vpdpwssd` lane layout (group `v = j/16` is one `<32 x i16>` vector, lane `l = j%16` in it consumes int16 elements `2l` and `2l+1`). The docstring said the split was "not a convenience" and my first model test asserted it DIFFERS from the naive `2*j + h`. It does not: `16*(j/16) + (j mod 16) = j`, so the whole thing collapses and the map **is** `2*j + h`. `slot_b_is_the_plain_interleave` states it as a theorem. So the gap is wider than the usual "bijectivity cannot tell two layouts apart" - **there are not two layouts**, there is no arithmetic content for any proof to capture, and the entire lane claim rests on `tests/cpu_gemm_vnni_micro.rs` running the real instruction. Asserting the EQUALITY is the stronger test anyway: the emitter carries the `32` and the `16` as separate literals and any inconsistent pair breaks it. **Check whether an expression you are about to call load-bearing actually simplifies.**
  - **REDUNDANT GUARDS CANNOT BE ISOLATED BY AN END-TO-END DIFFERENTIAL, and the sweep says which of five shapes is the only live one.** Removing a packer's mask and running all five shapes: `pack_a` alone 0 wrong everywhere, `pack_b` alone 0 wrong everywhere, BOTH -> 3763 at 53x71x301 and 6144 at 48x128x301 and **0 at the other three**. (a) The two masks are redundant with each other and no driver can separate them - a padding term is `a_pad * b_pad`, so a zero on either side kills it; removing one leaves the kernel correct and UNDEFENDED, not wrong, and the obligation actually pinned is the conjunction, which is what the theorem states. (b) **Only the phantom k-half can corrupt an answer**: ragged M and ragged N report 0 with both masks gone because those rows and columns are discarded by the C store mask first - `ExactGemmTiling.v`'s property doing double duty. So one shape is load-bearing and four are controls, and the test's docstring carries the table rather than implying five-fold coverage. The row/column masks are defence in depth against a future change to the store, recorded rather than deleted.
  - **A SURVIVOR IS A HYPOTHESIS ABOUT THE TEST - CHECK WHERE THE MUTATION LANDED.** Three "survivors" were mis-aimed: `s.replace(old, new, 1)` was hitting a DOCSTRING occurrence of the slot expression forty lines above the code. A fourth was worse - a mutation whose `cargo build` FAILED, leaving the previous binary in `target/release/`, so the driver ran and printed a perfectly clean `wrong 0`. **Assert the build succeeded before reading any result**, and target a mutation by line when the anchor text appears in prose as well as in code. 10/10 caught once aimed correctly.
  - **The fish word-splitting trap, hit for the second time in this repo.** `for s in "53 71 301" ...; do $exe $s` passes ONE argument in fish, so a five-shape sweep silently ran the driver's DEFAULT shape five times - and the mutation numbers looked identical across every shape, which is what gave it away. Identical results across a swept axis mean the axis is not being swept.

**The proof gate now sweeps `proofs/` instead of naming one file, which is exactly how the second proof would have gone unrun.** The original `tests/proofs_are_checked.rs` hardcoded `ZkControlFlow.v` — the same mistake it exists to prevent, one level up. A new `.v` gets all three checks automatically; the `Print Assumptions` count is taken from the SOURCE so deleting one cannot quietly shrink what is checked; and `every_proof_has_a_content_control` refuses to let a proof arrive without a named load-bearing theorem, because "compiles" and "no axioms" are properties an EMPTY file has.

**The Coq proof was run by a documented command and by nothing else (`tests/proofs_are_checked.rs`).** `proofs/ZkControlFlow.v` is the repo's only machine-checked artifact and no test, build script or CI job ran it — the same shape as `@ZeroDrift` before it was implemented and the `scheme = "plonkish"` flag. It matters more here because the proof is about a MODEL of the lowering rather than about `zk_emitter.rs`, so it can drift in silence. Three claims: `coqc` accepts it; every `Print Assumptions` reports `Closed under the global context` with no `Axioms:` section; nothing is `Admitted` (coqc accepts an admitted lemma and exits 0). Compiled in a temp directory, because `coqc` writes `.vo`/`.glob` beside the source and would race a developer running it by hand — the `.ptx` race again. Mutation-verified 4/4, and **the control is what makes it mean anything**: "no axioms" and "nothing admitted" are both properties an EMPTY file has, so a third test asserts `low_correct` and the nested-case refutation are still present and still under `Print Assumptions`.

**`let x: T = {}` had no PTX lowering, and the gate that found it was a DOCUMENTED COMMAND in a directory `cargo test` never runs.** One of the two documented Python test commands (`discover -s python/tests`) had been failing on `test_block_tile_boundary_masking_ptx`, whose kernel declares a tile as `let tile: BlockTile<F32, 128> = {};`. A zero-initialiser fell to `emit_expr`'s `_ => "".into()` and then to the "initialiser produced no value" refusal — while `type_checker` types it, `llvm_emitter` memsets it, and `tests/bounds_test.ysu` uses it. **The corpus sweep could not see it**: no `tests/*.ysu` uses `{}` inside a kernel, so the only caller was in `python/`, which lives in the stale outer clone and which `cargo test` does not touch.
  - Three cases, decided **before `emit_expr` runs** so a declaration is never asked to produce a value: a scalar gets `mov.<ty> %r, 0`; a `BlockTile` is a DECLARATION with nothing to emit and nothing to bind (the tile intrinsics take the buffer directly and never read the name — the same reason binding nothing is right for a linear token, and if the name IS read the `Expr::Ident` refusal now catches it); an array or struct is **refused by name**, because this backend has no local aggregate storage and zeroing "the array" would zero one scalar and call it the array.
  - **Attribute before claiming a regression.** The refusal appeared in the same session that added the `Expr::ZeroInit` refusal, and looked exactly like one. Building the PARENT commit in a worktree showed it refuses identically — the new arm only added a second, more precise message. Two minutes, and the alternative was reverting a correct change.
  - **A surviving mutation was a real finding, not a mis-aimed probe.** Breaking a `Type::Generic { base: "BlockTile" }` arm changed nothing: the parser produces `Type::BlockTile` directly, so that arm was dead. Removed rather than left untested — the spelling would now fall to the named refusal, which is fail-closed. Sort every survivor; this one was neither a test hole nor a confirmation but dead code.

**The conditional-gate audit came back CLEAN on this machine, and that is worth recording because it is usually where the bugs are.** `ptxas`, `z3` (via `venv/bin/z3`), `solcjs` (via `node_modules/.bin`), `circom`, `clang`, `rustc` and `coqc` are all present, and neither suite printed a single skip notice. The Solidity gate reports `ok` in **0.46 s**, which looks exactly like a silent skip — it is not: reversing the G2 `c0`/`c1` swap, the precise bug it exists to catch, fails it. **A suspicious timing is a hypothesis, and mutation is what settles it.** `coqc proofs/ZkControlFlow.v` and `coqchk` both pass with no axioms and nothing admitted, as documented.

**The COMMITTED ARTIFACTS carried the same bug, and a regeneration is not a gate (`tests/committed_ptx_artifacts.rs`).** Regenerating the corpus after the sweep above found **24 committed `.ptx` files that were a header and nothing else** — that bug's own output, checked in, referenced by no test, script or benchmark. It found a second class at the same time: **55 of the 59 committed artifacts at `.version 8.4` contain no FP8 instruction at all**, i.e. they demand CUDA 12.4 to run two `mov`s and fail to load on an 11.8 driver. This document already recorded the second one happening — "two committed artifacts were also still at 8.4 - the previous regeneration pass missed them, and no test could tell" — and the pass had missed **32**, not two.
  - **The gate is the deliverable; the sweep is a one-time act.** Two hermetic assertions, no GPU, no `ptxas`, no recompilation: no committed `.ptx` may contain zero instruction lines, and its `.version` must EQUAL the floor `ptx_version_for_sm` gives for its `.target`. This is the artifact twin of `backends_refuse_empty_artifacts` (which stops the backend PRODUCING one) and of `no_source_file_hardcodes_a_ptx_version_above_the_floor` (which covers source literals, never artifacts).
  - **It found three more on its first run that the sweep could not**: the `*.wrapped.ptx` benchmark outputs, still carrying the hardcoded `.version 8.0` from before the four Python harnesses were fixed to reuse the module's own header. That literal is over-stated on sm_89 and **rejected outright on Blackwell**. Deleted rather than regenerated — their producer rewrites them before every read, so they were never load-bearing. **A fixed producer does not fix the artifacts it already wrote**, which is the same observation as "fixing the ARTIFACTS is not fixing the COMPILER" read backwards.
  - The FP8 exemption is detected **per-instruction** (`e4m3`/`e5m2` present) rather than waved through by architecture, because a per-instruction requirement belongs on the module and not on the arch — and mutation confirms it is load-bearing rather than a blanket pass: four artifacts genuinely need 8.4.
  - The non-vacuity control matters as much as the two gates: a sweep that finds no files reports "none of them is empty" perfectly (`feedback-null-metrics-pass-dead-components`).

**Two harness errors of my own, worth more than either fix.** The shell here is fish, so `for a in "f.ysu --emit-ptx"; do Y $a` passes the whole string as ONE argument — every multi-token command reported "Failed to read file", which I first read as a refusal and nearly recorded as correct behaviour for `--emit-c`. And running the corpus sweep concurrently with `cargo test --release` relinks `target/release/Y` underneath it, producing failures that reproduce nowhere. **Re-run anything surprising serially, with the arguments passed explicitly, before believing it.**

**The empty-artifact sweep is complete across all six backends, and the two GPU-adjacent ones had MIRROR-IMAGE bugs.** `ptx_emitter::emit_program` matched `Item::Kernel` and dropped everything else; `native_emitter::emit_program` matched `Item::Func` and dropped everything else. Each backend kept only the half it understood and discarded the rest in silence — and neither could be seen by any gate, because the artifact each produced was well-formed.

| backend | what it emitted for input it could not handle |
|---|---|
| `--emit-llvm` | GPU types/intrinsics transcribed → invalid IR (11) and unresolvable symbols (10) |
| `--emit-cpu` | *already correct* — refused by name |
| `--emit-ptx` | a `.version`/`.target` header, no instructions (24 of 85) |
| `--emit-coprocessor` | a launchable `ret;` kernel with a fabricated signature (77 of 83) |
| `--target=r1cs` | a zero-constraint circuit (**57 of 57**) |
| `--emit-native` | a 162-byte no-op ELF, byte-identical to an empty program's |

The transferable part is the question, not the fixes: **for each backend, what does it do with input that belongs to a different backend?** Every one of these was reachable by typing a documented flag at a file already in `tests/`.

**The empty-artifact sweep found its worst case in the ZK backend, and the tell was a `fn main() {}` stub.** A `kernel` with no `main` at all is refused correctly — "No entry function 'main' or 'circuit' found" — so the shape looks safe until you notice that every generated GPU kernel in `tests/` ends with an empty `main` stub, and that stub converts a correct refusal into a **zero-constraint R1CS**. That is the one artifact this compiler must never emit under a success banner: an empty `.ptx` does nothing, an empty `.r1cs` *asserts* nothing while looking exactly like a circuit that does. Refused on the constraint count ALONE — a circuit with no public inputs is a legitimate proof of knowledge, and one with no outputs is a body of pure assertions, so neither may be caught by the same net.

**Two front ends means two arms, and the second one printed the number it was not checking.** The first version of that fix guarded the `.ysu` path only; an empty circom template still compiled clean, and `compile_circom` displays `circuit.constraints.len()` one line above the write. Both call one `refuse_if_no_constraints` now. Mutation confirms the split is real: guarding only the `.ysu` arm is caught by the circom test and by nothing else.

**An EMPTY artifact assembles, and that is the limit of every `ptxas` gate in this repo.** Gotcha #8 records that an assemble gate cannot see a *missing instruction*. Three rows above are the same observation one level up — the whole PROGRAM is missing. A corpus-wide `ptxas` sweep run immediately before that fix reported **82 of 82 accepted** while 24 of them contained no instructions at all, and `success_banner_means_success` is blind to it too: the banner and the exit code agree with each other, and both are wrong about the file. The only assertion that separates them is about CONTENT — `tests/backends_refuse_empty_artifacts.rs` counts instruction lines inside the entry (a real fused kernel has ~83, the fabricated one had 0), which is `feedback-decorative-codegen-passes-every-test`'s "assert the EFFECT not the vocabulary" applied to an artifact rather than to a pass.

Two process notes from that sweep, both worth more than the fixes:

- **Measure before building.** The corpus-wide `ptxas` sweep was run first *specifically* to find out whether a gate was worth writing. It said 82/82 clean — and the bug was hiding inside that number. The follow-up question ("how many of those modules contain anything?") is what found it. **When a sweep comes back perfect, ask what it would have looked like if the thing you are checking were absent.**
- **A refusal baseline is a list of unexamined bugs until you read it.** `coprocessor_nerf` looked like a false positive of the new check and was not — it was already refused, correctly, for needing 131,584 bytes of shared memory against the 48 KB static cap. Checking that took two minutes and would have been a wrong "fix" otherwise.

**The five newest rows are one session's sweep of the LLVM/host path, and the ordering they were found in is the lesson.** Running `clang` over every module the backend emits — the foreign-compiler oracle, applied to the LLVM backend the way rustc was applied to `--emit-cpu` — said **12 of 76 were invalid IR**. Fixing those exposed the next layer each time:

- **A sentinel collision is not a missing arm, and it discards the CORRECT answer.** `ast_type_to_llvm_type` returns `"i32"` for a genuine `I32`, an `Unknown` ast type, an empty one, an unregistered name, and a data-less enum. Its callers could not tell success from failure, so they treated `"i32"` as failure — and `&mut I32` is the language's commonest pointer. `&mut I64` was right all along, which is exactly why nobody noticed: **every `*x` in the corpus is `&mut I64` or `&mut String`, so the fix changes the emitted IR of ZERO of the 76 programs.** The bug was live and simply uncovered. When a function's success value and failure value are the same value, the caller cannot be correct — put the sentinel where the cases differ.
- **Refusing `*x` on a non-reference broke `--emit-cpu`, and rustc named the reason**: the parser had been discarding the `mut` in `&mut x` since forever. That one is worth reading because it was wrong in BOTH directions — refusing correct programs *and* accepting wrong ones — which is a shape that survives a long time, since each direction looks like the other's justification.
- **The corpus sweep does not subsume the narrow tests, and only mutation says so.** Dropping the `U32x4` type refusal leaves the sweep green, because every corpus program using that type also calls a GPU intrinsic and is refused by the *other* check first. The working path masks the broken one — the `mma_sync` lesson, in a test suite instead of an emitter.
- **Undoing the phase-0 split was caught by nothing.** Registering structs and resolving function signatures in one loop means `emit_type` is asked about a struct declared later in the file; no corpus program declares a function above the struct it returns, so a forward-reference fixture had to be written for it. A real test hole, found by mutation and closed.
- **A refusal's allowlist is a second copy of something, and it will drift.** The first version conflated "already declared in the prelude" with "exists in `c_src/runtime.c`", which suppressed the declaration for `String_new` and turned two VALID modules into invalid ones. `runtime_symbols_match_the_runtime` asserts the emitter's list AGREES with the runtime rather than re-deriving it — the `.version` gate's device — and the control asserts its OWN non-vacuity, because a fixture that stops reaching the auto-declare path guards nothing.

**"Compilation Successful!" was printed BEFORE the backend dispatch ran, so every backend failure was announced under a green banner.** `--emit-native` on an `if`, `--target=r1cs` on an out-of-range comparison operand: banner, then `[4/4]`, then a red error, then `exit(1)`. The exit code was always right and no artifact was ever written, so this is the *reporting* half of the failure shape rather than a correctness bug - but it is the same reading error that `wgmma_async`, the plonkish scheme flag and the silently-ignored `--c` all depend on. The pre-dispatch line is `Front-end analysis complete.` now and the real banner moved to the end of `main`, which every successful path falls through to (no arm exits 0).
  - `tests/success_banner_means_success.rs` pins the **biconditional**: the banner appears iff the exit code is 0. "Never print it" satisfies half of that and is useless - the success control is what makes the file mean anything, the same shape as `ordinary_loop_bodies_still_verify`. Mutation-verified in both directions.
  - **It immediately exposed four tests in three files using the banner as a proxy for "the front end accepted this program"** - they compile stubs calling undeclared functions, or use `match`, which the PTX backend refuses by name. They assert on the front-end line now. Their NEGATIVE assertions got STRONGER in the same move: `!contains(banner)` was previously satisfied by a program the front end ACCEPTED and a backend then refused, which reads as "the front end rejected it".

**There is a cross-backend differential now (`tests/backend_differential.rs`), and it found a bug on its first run.** This document already said, about the ZK `return` bug, that "the LLVM backend compiles the same program to `ret i32 1`, so the two backends disagreed on what `return` means — a cross-backend differential is the cheapest test that would have caught it". Nobody had written one. It generates straight-line integer programs, compiles them through **both** `--emit-llvm` and `--emit-native`, runs both binaries, and compares: **6 of 40 disagreed**, all on comparison operators, because `emit_coerce` sign-extended the `i1` an `icmp` produces. `--emit-native`, the ZK emitter (booleanity-constrained) and `cpu_emitter` (a Rust `bool`) all answer 1; LLVM alone answered -1. **A differential is the only test shape that can find "which of my backends is the odd one out" without anyone deciding in advance what the answer should be.**
  - **A process exit status carries 8 bits**, so one program compares one byte of a 32-bit answer. Each generated program returns `(expr >> s) & 255` for `s` drawn from {0, 8, 16, 24}, spreading the comparison over the word. This leans on `>>` and `&` agreeing, which is itself under test — and a bug present *identically* in both backends is invisible to any differential, which is the standing limit of the technique.
  - **Refusals are counted, not skipped.** `--emit-native` refuses everything outside its subset, so a generator that drifted out of it would leave the differential comparing nothing and passing. `the_corpus_is_not_all_skips` asserts a floor (currently 40/40 compare, 0 refused). Same lesson as `feedback-null-metrics-pass-dead-components`.
  - Its two tests raced each other on identical temp-dir names and presented as an intermittent failure **with no disagreement listed** — the `.ptx` race from the GPU harness, in a new file, on the first run.
  - **Deepening the generator found a second bug the flat one could not.** `emit_coerce`'s promotion only runs when the two operand types DIFFER, so two comparisons combined by a third operator stayed at `i1`, where LLVM reads `1` as -1: `((v == v) < (v > v))` emitted `icmp slt i1 1, 0` and answered TRUE. `add i1` wraps mod 2 as well, so `(a > b) + (c > d)` could only ever be 0 or 1. 400 flat programs had already passed clean — a flat program cannot put a comparison in an operand position. **The fix is two sites**: widening in the emitter alone left `infer_type` still reporting `i1`, so the caller emitted `zext i1 %t` on an i32 register and clang rejected the module.
  - That in turn exposed the vacuous-skip hole in `tests/llvm_integer_widths.rs`, whose `run_program` returned `None` for both "no clang" and "clang rejected the IR" — so the `infer_type` mutation initially SURVIVED with the whole file green. Hardened the same way `llvm_control_flow.rs` was. **Three files have now had this exact harness bug; check it in any helper that returns an `Option` for a build.**

**`tests/zk_llvm_differential.rs` is the same idea reaching CONTROL FLOW, which the native pairing cannot** (the native backend has no branches). The same body is compiled to a binary by LLVM and to an R1CS circuit solved for its witness by `zk_emitter`, with the inputs as PARAMETERS on both sides so neither can fold a condition away. Field-vs-`i32` differences are designed out rather than tolerated: no subtraction is generated (`3 - 5` is `p - 2` in the field), and every binding is masked to 16 bits so no product can pass `i32`.
  - **It is validated by re-introducing each of the four historical control-flow bugs, not by assertion.** "`return` not a terminator" and "`Stmt::For` discards its body's return" are CAUGHT. "The condition is never constrained to a bit" is NOT, and that is a confirmation rather than a hole — every generated condition is a comparison, which already yields a booleanity-constrained bit. The Coq-found one has no shape left to restore.
  - **The `for` bug was missed twice before it was caught**, which is the transferable part. First the generator emitted no loops; then it emitted loops whose guard compared a raw parameter (0..199) against an index below 5, so the return inside could never be taken and the mutation stayed green. A branch that cannot be reached tests nothing — `feedback-exercised-is-not-covered`, one level down.
  - **Building it found a live bug in a feature the compiler was recommending: `while` with `@max_iterations(N)` computed the wrong function, and is now REFUSED.** The bounded form unrolled N times behind an active mask (`active_{i+1} = active_i * cond_{i+1}`, every mutated variable muxed on it) and failed three ways depending on the bound. `while i < p0 { acc = acc + 3; i = i + 1; }`, solved for p0 = 0..3: **`@max_iterations(1)` gives 3, 3, 3, 3 where the answer is 0, 3, 3, 3** — the body ran although the condition was false on entry, the circuit is SATISFIABLE, and Groth16 proves it; `@max_iterations(2)` is **correct**; `@max_iterations(4)` is unsatisfiable for every non-zero input. **That N=2 is correct is how it survived** — it is what anyone probes first. Refused rather than repaired, and the lowering kept as dead code behind the refusal.
    - Its unit test asserted the emitted text contains `active_mask` and that constraints exist. Both hold perfectly for a circuit computing the wrong function: **a substring test pinning a broken construct as a regression guard**, the `wgmma...s4` mistake again, in the backend where the artifact is a proof.
    - The docs advertised it in two places and are corrected with the measured table rather than quietly edited. `@max_iterations` still parses for other backends.



**`SemanticType::Unknown` is not a neutral answer in `type_checker`, and three arms were returning it.** The `let` arm reads `Unknown` as "adopt the annotation" and the assignment arm exempts it from the mismatch check outright — so `Unknown` on *either* side of a comparison silently suppresses it. `Type::Reference` and every `Expr::UnaryOp` both returned it, which meant `let r: &F32 = &x;` with `x: I32` was unchecked on both sides. **Fixing either alone buys nothing**, and mutation shows worse than nothing: repairing only the annotation makes the CORRECT case (`&I32 = &x`) start being refused. When a check compares two derived values, both derivations are the fix.

**The five newest rows are all in code that NOTHING GATED, and they split into two kinds.** `quantization_pass` is live — it sits on `coprocessor_scheduler`'s `needs_quantization` path, the same `cross_pipeline_edges()` loop as the two `ir_grapher` rows below, so the fix there made these fire more often. `auto_vectorize` and `rocm_emitter` were dead and are deleted.

**A decorative code generator passes every test this repo had.** Gotcha #8 says PTX tests must assemble rather than string-match; that is necessary and not sufficient, because *comments assemble* and so does `mov.u32 %qr, 0`. Of the seven precision pairs the quantization pass claimed, four emit a real `cvt` instruction and are still wrong — they never emit a **store**, so shared memory keeps the source bits and the tensor core reinterprets them. The assertion that separates real from decorative is therefore about the output's EFFECT, not its vocabulary:

    strip comments and blank lines; require what remains to contain `st.shared`

That one line found all five. `tests/quantization_pass_refuses.rs` pairs it with the refusal census (54 unimplemented pairs must be refused BY NAME) and a control (an identity conversion must be a legal no-op, not a refusal — refusing everything unimplemented is sound and useless, the same shape as `ordinary_loop_bodies_still_verify`).

**`run_all_optimization_passes` had zero callers and ran five passes, none of which did what its name said** — two renamed calls to intrinsics that exist in no backend, two counted and returned, one mutated nothing. They are deleted rather than fixed, because every one is superseded by something real (`bank_conflict.rs` for the swizzle, `block_ptr2d_load_v4` for the vector loads, `CpuShapeDispatcher` for the classification). **The mechanism that hid all of it is that 31 of the crate's modules open with a blanket `#![allow(dead_code)]`**, and `pub` items in a `pub mod` are never dead-code-flagged anyway — so neither rustc nor any test could have said a word. A liveness probe (run the pass, compare the AST before and after) is four lines and settles it; write one for any pass you cannot point at a caller for.

**The two `ir_grapher` rows are the newest, and they are the first found in a pass whose output is a SCHEDULE rather than an artifact.** Nothing downstream can catch them: the emitted PTX is well-formed, `ptxas` accepts it, and the kernel launches — it just overlaps two ops that depend on each other. Measured on `--emit-coprocessor` before the fix, the same program written two ways:

    b  = bvh_traverse(a);   RT 2  Tensor 1  cross-pipe 1  412 cycles  1 sync barrier
    b += bvh_traverse(a);   RT 1  Tensor 1  cross-pipe 0  212 cycles  0 sync barriers

**The barrier count is the real consequence, and it is worse than a bad cost estimate.** `coprocessor_scheduler::schedule` iterates `graph.cross_pipeline_edges()` to emit `SyncBarrier`s, and that same loop sets `needs_quantization`. Zero edges therefore means the emitted kernel has **no synchronisation between the RT producer and the Tensor consumer** *and* never converts FP32 to FP16 for the tensor core — a race and a type reinterpretation, from writing `+=` instead of `=`. Check what CONSUMES the structure a pass builds before ranking the severity of a hole in it.

`analyze_stmt` handled 10 of 17 `Stmt` variants; the four that mattered were `CompoundAssign` (no node, no edge, and **`var_producers` left pointing at the previous producer** — so a later consumer wires to a stale node), `Match` (arm bodies never walked — the same site-not-variant gap the linear tracker had for `match`), `Return` (its expression still executes), and `ClockDomainBlock` (every other block-carrying statement was walked). `wire_expr_dependencies` handled 5 of 17 `Expr` variants and dropped four sub-expression carriers, `StructLit` among them — the same variant that hid the `takes_reference` gap.
  - The regression test asserts an **equivalence, not a count**: `x += e` is `x = x + e`, so the two must graph identically. A count would need updating whenever the cost model moves; the equivalence holds as long as the language does. Gated by `tests/ir_grapher_dependency_coverage.rs`, mutation-verified 7/7.
  - **Its first version was named `a_read_through_a_struct_field_is_still_a_dependency` and never built a struct literal** — it asserted on a plain call and passed with the `StructLit` arm mutated back to `=> {}`. Caught by running the mutation, not by reading the test. A test named for the case it does not exercise is worse than no test, because it retires the question.

**The two rows above `native_emitter` are one finding in two layers, and the order they were found in is the point.** `ptx_emitter::emit_stmt` had no `Stmt::While` arm, so a `while` loop in a kernel emitted NOTHING — and no `ptxas` gate could see it, because a missing instruction assembles perfectly (gotcha #8 again). It survived because it was **unreachable**: `check_stmt` clears the interval of every body-assigned variable before verifying a loop, and the INITIATION obligation is about the state on ENTRY where those intervals are still true, so every `@invariant` naming a body-assigned variable failed — and a `while`'s induction variable always is one. An `@invariant` is mandatory outside `unsafe`, so no `while` loop in safe Y reached a backend at all. `tests/math.ysu` and `tests/safe_test.ysu` were both refused by it; the corpus went **78 compile / 5 refuse to 80 / 3**. Fixing the front-end check is what made the backend gap live, within the same hour.
  - The fix is a snapshot of the pre-loop intervals threaded into the initiation query **only**, and that narrowness has its own test.
